question: Why are hormonal contraceptives or cyclical progestins often prescribed for women with chronic amenorrhoea?

options.A: To stimulate immediate ovulation in the ovaries
options.B: To increase basal body temperature permanently
options.C: To permanently cure the underlying hypothalamic defect
options.D: To prevent endometrial hyperplasia from unopposed estrogen

explanation: Regular shedding of the uterine lining protects against abnormal thickening and cellular changes. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T4#GNS216_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is a major long-term complication of prolonged hypo-oestrogenic amenorrhoea?

options.A: Uterine fibroids
options.B: Cervical stenosis
options.C: Osteoporosis
options.D: Gestational diabetes

explanation: Estrogen protects bone density; its prolonged absence significantly increases the risk of brittle bones and fractures. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T4#GNS216_U2_T4_h7)

question: How does chronic anovulation affect the endometrium over time?

options.A: It exposes the tissue to unopposed estrogen and potential hyperplasia
options.B: It leads to continuous shedding without hormonal control
options.C: It triggers localized inflammation and pelvic adhesions
options.D: It causes the uterine lining to thin out completely

explanation: Without progesterone to balance estrogen, the endometrium continuously thickens, raising the risk of abnormal cellular growth. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T4#GNS216_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is an important psychosocial concern for many women experiencing amenorrhoea?

options.A: Anxiety about daily injections
options.B: Concerns about future fertility
options.C: Distress over surgical scars
options.D: Fear of sudden weight gain

explanation: Many women associate regular menstruation directly with their ability to conceive, leading to anxiety when it stops. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T4#GNS216_U2_T4_h8)

question: How should the nurse best support a patient recovering from exercise-induced amenorrhoea?

options.A: Advise her to stop all physical activity permanently
options.B: Reassure her that the condition requires no lifestyle changes
options.C: Focus exclusively on pharmacological treatment options
options.D: Discuss healthy adjustments to caloric intake and training intensity

explanation: Addressing the energy deficit through balanced nutrition and modified exercise restores hormonal balance naturally. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T4#GNS216_U2_T4_h8)

question: What is the minimum cycle length in days that defines oligomenorrhoea?

options.A: 50 days
options.B: 90 days
options.C: 21 days
options.D: 35 days

explanation: Cycles lasting longer than 35 days but under 90 days are classified as oligomenorrhoea. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h1)

question: How many menstrual periods per year does a woman with oligomenorrhoea typically experience?

options.A: Exactly 12 periods
options.B: Less than 9 periods
options.C: Zero periods
options.D: More than 15 periods

explanation: Infrequent cycles exceeding 35 days result in an annual total of fewer than nine menstrual episodes. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which gland releases Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone to stimulate the HPO axis?

options.A: Adrenal cortex
options.B: Hypothalamus
options.C: Anterior pituitary
options.D: Ovary

explanation: The hypothalamus is responsible for the pulsatile release of GnRH, which drives downstream hormonal activity. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the direct consequence of a disrupted communication cascade within the HPO axis?

options.A: Altered ovulation and delayed shedding
options.B: Permanent enlargement of the ovaries
options.C: Instantaneous atrophy of the myometrium
options.D: Immediate complete cessation of all hormones

explanation: Disruption in the axis prevents timely ovulation, causing delayed endometrial shedding and longer cycles. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the most common endocrine cause of oligomenorrhoea in clinical practice?

options.A: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
options.B: Primary ovarian failure
options.C: Cushing's syndrome
options.D: Diabetes insipidus

explanation: PCOS is widely recognized as the primary endocrine driver behind chronic anovulatory cycles. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h3)

question: How does chronic psychological or physical stress lead to infrequent menses?

options.A: It directly blocks the cervical os
options.B: It causes severe endometrial fibrosis
options.C: It suppresses hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility
options.D: It destroys ovarian follicular reserves instantly

explanation: Stress impacts the brain centers, dampening GnRH secretion and halting regular downstream stimulation. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which initial test must be performed during the evaluation of delayed menses to rule out pregnancy?

options.A: Full blood count
options.B: Serum beta-hCG
options.C: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.D: Liver function test

explanation: Ruling out pregnancy is always the first diagnostic step when evaluating any form of menstrual irregularity. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h4)

question: A patient with oligomenorrhoea also presents with dark, velvety skin patches on her neck. What physical sign is this?

options.A: Galactorrhoea
options.B: Acanthosis nigricans
options.C: Hirsutism
options.D: Exophthalmos

explanation: Acanthosis nigricans is a cutaneous marker closely linked to insulin resistance, commonly seen in PCOS. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why are combined oral contraceptives often prescribed for women with chronic oligomenorrhoea?

options.A: To stimulate immediate natural ovulation
options.B: To permanently cure underlying pituitary adenomas
options.C: To protect the endometrium from unopposed estrogen
options.D: To lower circulating thyroid hormone levels

explanation: Regular progestogen exposure from contraceptives prevents endometrial hyperplasia caused by constant, unopposed estrogen. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h5)

question: Which medication is commonly used to improve insulin sensitivity in patients with PCOS-related oligomenorrhoea?

options.A: Levothyroxine
options.B: Insulin glargine
options.C: Cabergoline
options.D: Metformin

explanation: Metformin helps manage insulin resistance, which often helps restore ovulation in women with PCOS. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the primary long-term uterine risk associated with untreated chronic anovulation?

options.A: Myometrial leiomyosarcoma
options.B: Endometrial hyperplasia and carcinoma
options.C: Atrophic vaginitis and stenosis
options.D: Cervical dysplasia and cancer

explanation: Unopposed estrogen stimulation over long periods causes the uterine lining to overgrow, leading to hyperplasia and potential malignancy. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which metabolic condition is commonly linked as a long-term impact in women with untreated PCOS?

options.A: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
options.B: Chronic kidney disease
options.C: Obstructive sleep apnea
options.D: Rheumatoid arthritis

explanation: Insulin resistance tied to conditions like PCOS elevates the long-term risk of developing type 2 diabetes. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is an effective practical tool a nurse should teach a patient to monitor her cycle irregularities?

options.A: Weighing herself once every two weeks
options.B: Keeping a detailed menstrual calendar
options.C: Measuring daily core body temperature only
options.D: Checking random blood glucose twice daily

explanation: A menstrual calendar helps patients track cycle length accurately and provides vital data for clinical review. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h7)

question: Why is emotional and psychological support a critical component of nursing care for oligomenorrhoea?

options.A: Psychological counseling replaces the need for hormone therapy
options.B: Fertility struggles can cause significant social and emotional distress
options.C: Anxiety directly cures pituitary tumors without medication
options.D: Mental stress is the sole cause of all menstrual disorders

explanation: Societal pressures regarding childbearing mean that irregular cycles and associated subfertility often cause deep emotional distress. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is the medical term for painful menstrual cramps?

options.A: Metrorrhagia
options.B: Menorrhagia
options.C: Amenorrhoea
options.D: Dysmenorrhoea

explanation: Dysmenorrhoea specifically refers to the occurrence of painful cramps during menstruation. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h1)

question: How does severe dysmenorrhoea typically affect a young woman's daily routine?

options.A: It completely stops the normal menstrual flow
options.B: It disrupts school attendance and normal activities
options.C: It causes permanent damage to the reproductive organs
options.D: It triggers sudden weight gain and high blood pressure

explanation: Intense pelvic pain and cramping often interfere with a student's ability to attend classes and perform daily tasks. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h1)

question: Primary dysmenorrhoea is best defined as menstrual pain occurring without what factor?

options.A: Identifiable pelvic pathology
options.B: Regular ovulation cycles
options.C: Family history of cramps
options.D: Normal hormonal balance

explanation: Primary dysmenorrhoea happens independently of any structural disease or recognizable pelvic abnormality. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h2)

question: A 35-year-old woman develops worsening menstrual pain due to uterine fibroids. What condition does she have?

options.A: Primary dysmenorrhoea
options.B: Physiological amenorrhoea
options.C: Premenstrual syndrome
options.D: Secondary dysmenorrhoea

explanation: When menstrual pain is caused by a distinct structural problem like fibroids, it is classified as secondary dysmenorrhoea. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h2)

question: Which chemical messenger is primarily responsible for causing uterine contractions in dysmenorrhoea?

options.A: Prostaglandins
options.B: Histamine
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Thyroxine

explanation: Elevated levels of prostaglandins in the endometrium stimulate strong contractions of the uterine muscle during menses. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h3)

question: Why does excessive prostaglandin release lead to ischemic pain in the uterine muscle?

options.A: It dilates pelvic blood vessels and lowers systemic blood pressure
options.B: It causes intense vasoconstriction that reduces local blood supply
options.C: It blocks nerve impulses traveling from the spinal cord
options.D: It increases the core body temperature during ovulation

explanation: Strong vasoconstriction cuts down oxygen delivery to the myometrium, resulting in ischemia-induced cramping pain. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h3)

question: During which timeframe do dysmenorrhoea symptoms usually reach their peak intensity?

options.A: Immediately after the menstrual flow stops
options.B: Right at the midpoint of the menstrual cycle
options.C: Two weeks before the bleeding begins
options.D: Within the first twenty-four hours of menses

explanation: Prostaglandin release is highest during the first day of menstruation, causing cramps to peak early in the cycle. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which symptom is commonly associated with dysmenorrhoea alongside lower abdominal pain?

options.A: Involuntary muscle tremors
options.B: Nausea and fatigue
options.C: Severe chest pain
options.D: Sudden skin jaundice

explanation: Systemic prostaglandin spillover into the bloodstream frequently provokes nausea, vomiting, and generalized fatigue. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is a recognized risk factor for developing primary dysmenorrhoea?

options.A: Late onset of puberty
options.B: High daily water intake
options.C: Low body mass index
options.D: Early age at menarche

explanation: Girls who experience their first menstrual period at an early age have a higher statistical risk of developing dysmenorrhoea. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h5)

question: When should a nurse suspect secondary dysmenorrhoea instead of primary dysmenorrhoea during an assessment?

options.A: When cramps begin precisely on the very first day of bleeding
options.B: When pain disappears completely after using a simple hot water bottle
options.C: When pelvic pain starts later in life and progressively worsens
options.D: When the patient reports feeling mild fatigue during her period

explanation: New-onset or worsening pain in older reproductive years often points toward an underlying structural pathology. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h5)

question: Which medication class is considered first-line medical treatment for primary dysmenorrhoea?

options.A: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
options.B: Broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: Opioid pain relievers
options.D: Skeletal muscle relaxants

explanation: NSAIDs directly inhibit prostaglandin production, making them the primary choice for managing menstrual cramps. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h6)

question: How do hormonal contraceptives help relieve severe menstrual pain?

options.A: By increasing local blood flow and raising systemic body temperature
options.B: By suppressing ovulation and decreasing endometrial tissue growth
options.C: By blocking pain receptors directly in the central nervous system
options.D: By stimulating the production of high levels of natural progesterone

explanation: Contraceptives reduce the amount of lining available to produce prostaglandins during menstruation. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h6)

question: What is the best advice a nurse can give regarding the timing of NSAID administration for dysmenorrhoea?

options.A: Use the drugs strictly during the middle of the ovulation cycle
options.B: Only take the medicine on the final day of the menstrual flow
options.C: Take the medication just as the menstrual period or pain begins
options.D: Wait until the pain becomes unbearable before taking any pills

explanation: Taking NSAIDs early prevents the buildup of prostaglandins and provides much more effective pain relief. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h7)

question: Which nursing action is most appropriate when caring for a client experiencing acute menstrual cramps?

options.A: Instructing the client to avoid all forms of fluid intake
options.B: Demonstrating the use of local heat therapy to the abdomen
options.C: Administering prescribed intravenous antibiotics immediately
options.D: Recommending strict bed rest throughout the entire cycle

explanation: Applying a warm compress or hot water bottle helps relax the uterine muscles and eases cramping discomfort. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T6#GNS216_U2_T6_h7)

question: What is the primary product of spermatogenesis?

options.A: Mature spermatozoa
options.B: Testosterone hormone
options.C: Primitive germ cells
options.D: Primary spermatocytes

explanation: Spermatogenesis specifically refers to the developmental process that culminates in the formation of mature sperm cells. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h1)

question: Why is the reduction of genetic material during spermatogenesis biologically important?

options.A: It maintains the correct chromosome number upon fertilization
options.B: It speeds up the rate at which sperm cells mature
options.C: It prevents testosterone from destroying developing germ cells
options.D: It allows the sperm to swim faster in seminal fluid

explanation: Creating haploid cells ensures that when sperm combines with an ovum, the resulting zygote has the correct diploid chromosome count. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h1)

question: Where does actual sperm production take place inside the testicle?

options.A: Epididymis head
options.B: Seminiferous tubules
options.C: Scrotal sac lining
options.D: Vas deferens wall

explanation: The coiled seminiferous tubules provide the specialized microenvironment necessary for germ cells to divide and transform into sperm. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h2)

question: What is the clinical purpose of the scrotum hanging outside the main body cavity?

options.A: It maintains a cooler temperature required for normal sperm production
options.B: It allows the vas deferens to shorten during heavy physical labor
options.C: It protects the testicles from sudden physical trauma during walking
options.D: It increases blood circulation to speed up testosterone clearance

explanation: Sperm development is sensitive to heat and requires a temperature slightly lower than core body temperature. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h2)

question: Which gland releases Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone to start the reproductive axis?

options.A: Testicular Leydig cell
options.B: Hypothalamus
options.C: Anterior pituitary
options.D: Adrenal cortex

explanation: The hypothalamus acts as the master controller by releasing GnRH, which signals the pituitary gland to release reproductive hormones. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h3)

question: A patient with a pituitary tumor has low FSH levels. What is the direct consequence for this patient?

options.A: Excessive production of immature red blood cells
options.B: Complete absence of secondary sex characteristics
options.C: Immediate shrinkage of the scrotal sac muscles
options.D: Impaired support and nourishment of developing sperm cells

explanation: FSH directly stimulates Sertoli cells, which provide the essential structural and nutritional support needed for spermatogenesis. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h3)

question: During which phase of spermatogenesis does chromosome reduction occur?

options.A: Mitosis
options.B: Meiosis
options.C: Spermiogenesis
options.D: Capacitation

explanation: Meiosis is the specialized cell division process that halves the genetic material, producing haploid spermatids from diploid precursors. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary physical change that happens during spermiogenesis?

options.A: Primary spermatocytes duplicate their DNA inside the seminiferous tubules
options.B: Round spermatids transform into streamlined, tail-bearing spermatozoa
options.C: Stem cell spermatogonia multiply rapidly to increase reserve volume
options.D: Mature sperm mix with seminal fluids in the ejaculatory ducts

explanation: Spermiogenesis is the final maturation phase where the round spermatid remodels its shape and grows a flagellum for motility. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h4)

question: What is the main function of testicular Leydig cells?

options.A: Phagocytizing defective sperm cells
options.B: Synthesizing testosterone
options.C: Forming the blood-testis barrier
options.D: Propelling sperm into the epididymis

explanation: Leydig cells located in the interstitial tissue are responsible for producing the primary male sex hormone, testosterone. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h5)

question: Why is the blood-testis barrier created by Sertoli cells clinically important?

options.A: It prevents testosterone from leaking back into the systemic circulation
options.B: It prevents the body's immune system from attacking developing sperm as foreign
options.C: It filters out harmful bacteria coming directly from the bloodstream
options.D: It stores mature sperm until ejaculation is triggered by the nervous system

explanation: Because developing sperm express unique surface antigens, the blood-testis barrier isolates them from autoimmune destruction. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h5)

question: How does a varicocele negatively impact male fertility?

options.A: It blocks the vas deferens and prevents sperm from exiting the body
options.B: It destroys the anterior pituitary gland and halts FSH production
options.C: It raises the local temperature in the scrotum due to abnormal blood pooling
options.D: It triggers an immediate autoimmune attack against mature sperm cells

explanation: Varicoceles involve enlarged veins in the scrotum, which increase local heat and negatively affect sensitive sperm-producing cells. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h6)

question: Which viral infection is known to cause severe inflammation of the testes and subsequent infertility?

options.A: Tuberculosis
options.B: Mumps
options.C: Cholera
options.D: Malaria

explanation: Mumps orchitis is a well-known viral complication that can damage testicular tissue and impair future spermatogenesis. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h6)

question: A patient asks a nurse how to reduce lifestyle risks for poor sperm quality. What advice should the nurse provide?

options.A: Increase intake of caffeinated beverages to stimulate testicular blood flow
options.B: Sleep on the back with legs elevated to drain the scrotal veins
options.C: Avoid tight-fitting underwear and prolonged exposure to high scrotal heat
options.D: Take daily over-the-counter anti-inflammatory drugs to protect germ cells

explanation: Minimizing scrotal heat stress helps maintain optimal thermal conditions for normal sperm production. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h7)

question: What is an important component of a nursing assessment for male reproductive health?

options.A: Testing visual acuity to rule out pituitary tumor pressure
options.B: Palpating the abdominal aorta for signs of aneurysmal swelling
options.C: Checking deep tendon reflexes in the lower extremities daily
options.D: Inquiring about history of testicular trauma or mumps infection

explanation: Past trauma or infections like orchitis are key clinical indicators that can explain impaired spermatogenesis. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T7#GNS216_U2_T7_h7)

question: What is a major reason male patients delay seeking treatment for sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Mandatory quarantine policies in local clinics
options.B: Social stigma associated with sexual health
options.C: Lack of available diagnostic laboratories
options.D: Automatic immunity without medical intervention

explanation: Stigma creates a psychological barrier that discourages men from visiting healthcare facilities for STI symptoms. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h1)

question: Why do asymptomatic men present a unique challenge in STI control?

options.A: They develop chronic kidney failure much faster
options.B: They require immediate surgical intervention in theatre
options.C: They transmit infections to partners without knowing
options.D: They always test negative on laboratory blood panels

explanation: Individuals without visible symptoms continue normal sexual activities, unintentionally spreading pathogens within the community. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h1)

question: Which bacterium is responsible for causing classic gonorrhoea in men?

options.A: Escherichia coli
options.B: Chlamydia trachomatis
options.C: Treponema pallidum
options.D: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

explanation: Neisseria gonorrhoeae is a gram-negative diplococcus that specifically targets mucosal surfaces of the male urethra. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h2)

question: What type of pathogen causes primary syphilis in male patients?

options.A: A flagellated protozoan
options.B: An encapsulated fungus
options.C: A spirochete bacterium
options.D: A double-stranded DNA virus

explanation: Treponema pallidum is a spiral-shaped bacterium, known as a spirochete, that invades through broken skin or mucous membranes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h2)

question: What symptom is most characteristic of male urethritis?

options.A: Diffuse rash across the abdomen
options.B: High fever and severe joint pain
options.C: Painful urination and discharge
options.D: Painless swelling of the testicles

explanation: Inflammation of the urethral mucosa directly causes dysuria alongside visible urethral discharge. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h3)

question: A patient presenting with a single painless genital ulcer most likely has which infection?

options.A: Primary syphilis
options.B: Gonococcal infection
options.C: Chlamydial urethritis
options.D: Herpes genitalis

explanation: The primary chancre of syphilis is classically firm, round, and painless, unlike the painful grouped vesicles of herpes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h3)

question: What non-invasive specimen is commonly used for NAAT testing in men?

options.A: 24-hour pooled urine collection
options.B: Random midstream urine sample
options.C: Suprapubic bladder aspiration
options.D: First-void urine sample

explanation: The initial stream of urine washes out urethral pathogens, making it ideal for sensitive amplification tests. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h4)

question: Why is the VDRL blood test ordered during an STI evaluation?

options.A: To screen for antibodies against syphilis
options.B: To detect active gonococcal bacterial growth
options.C: To measure the CD4 count in HIV patients
options.D: To check renal clearance before antibiotic therapy

explanation: VDRL is a standard serological screening test that detects specific reagin antibodies produced in response to Treponema pallidum infection. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h4)

question: What is the primary nursing responsibility regarding prescribed antibiotic regimens?

options.A: Doubling doses if a single pill is missed
options.B: Stopping drugs once symptoms disappear
options.C: Switching medications to herbal alternatives
options.D: Emphasizing completion of the full course

explanation: Patients must finish all prescribed antibiotics to ensure complete eradication of the pathogen and prevent drug resistance. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h5)

question: Why is partner notification considered a vital component of STI care?

options.A: It prevents reinfection and breaks transmission cycles
options.B: It eliminates the need for laboratory investigations
options.C: It satisfies mandatory hospital administrative records
options.D: It guarantees immunity against future bacterial strains

explanation: Treating sexual partners simultaneously stops the ping-pong spread of infections between couples. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h5)

question: What is a localized structural complication of chronic untreated urethritis in men?

options.A: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
options.B: Bladder stone formation
options.C: Urethral stricture
options.D: Testicular hydrocele

explanation: Persistent inflammation and scarring of the urethral tissue lead to narrowing of the lumen, termed a stricture. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h6)

question: How do untreated ulcerative STIs impact a patient's systemic vulnerability?

options.A: They lead to spontaneous bone mineralization loss
options.B: They cause permanent systemic hypertension
options.C: They trigger immediate acute renal failure episodes
options.D: They increase the risk of acquiring HIV infection

explanation: Breaks in the mucosal barrier caused by ulcers provide a direct portal of entry for viruses like HIV. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h6)

question: Which measure offers the most reliable physical barrier against STI transmission?

options.A: Daily oral vitamin supplementation
options.B: Consistent barrier condom use
options.C: Frequent intake of herbal tonics
options.D: Routine post-exposure handwashing

explanation: Barrier methods physically block the exchange of infectious genital secretions and contact with lesions. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h7)

question: Why are nurse-led community health talks crucial for adolescent males?

options.A: They provide permanent immunity against all bacteria
options.B: They promote safe practices and encourage early testing
options.C: They replace the need for clinical diagnostic testing
options.D: They diagnose active urethral infections instantly

explanation: Education empowers young people with knowledge about transmission risks and motivates them to seek help promptly. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h7)

question: What is the primary bacterial species found in a healthy adult vagina?

options.A: Candida albicans
options.B: Lactobacilli species
options.C: Staphylococcus aureus
options.D: Escherichia coli

explanation: Lactobacilli are the dominant normal flora that maintain vaginal health by producing lactic acid and keeping the pH low. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h1)

question: Why is an acidic pH important for the normal vaginal environment?

options.A: It directly stimulates estrogen production in the ovaries
options.B: It helps the body absorb oral contraceptive pills
options.C: It prevents the overgrowth of harmful pathogens
options.D: It neutralizes alkaline menstrual blood instantly

explanation: The acidic pH creates a hostile environment that stops opportunistic bacteria and fungi from multiplying uncontrollably. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h1)

question: A thick, white, cottage-cheese-like vaginal discharge is most characteristic of which condition?

options.A: Vulvovaginal candidiasis
options.B: Bacterial vaginosis
options.C: Atrophic vaginitis
options.D: Trichomoniasis

explanation: Fungal infections caused by Candida species classically present with thick, white, clumpy discharge and intense itching. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h2)

question: A patient presents with a frothy yellow-green vaginal discharge and severe local irritation. What is the likely causative organism?

options.A: Candida albicans
options.B: Lactobacillus acidophilus
options.C: Trichomonas vaginalis
options.D: Gardnerella vaginalis

explanation: Trichomoniasis is a protozoan infection that typically manifests with a frothy, yellow-green discharge and is managed as a sexually transmitted infection. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h2)

question: How do broad-spectrum antibiotics commonly lead to a secondary vaginal infection?

options.A: By lowering systemic blood pressure and reducing pelvic blood flow
options.B: By changing the anatomical structure of the vaginal wall
options.C: By destroying protective lactobacilli and allowing yeast to overgrow
options.D: By directly increasing the production of cervical mucus

explanation: Antibiotics clear out good bacteria along with the bad ones, removing competition and allowing fungi like Candida to multiply. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h3)

question: Which practice directly disrupts the normal vaginal pH by washing away protective flora?

options.A: Frequent douching
options.B: Drinking adequate water
options.C: Consuming yoghurt daily
options.D: Wearing cotton underwear

explanation: Douching flushes out the normal resident bacteria and alters the acidic balance, making the vagina prone to infections. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h3)

question: Why does the characteristic odor of bacterial vaginosis often worsen after sexual intercourse?

options.A: Alkaline semen reacts with amines produced by anaerobic bacteria
options.B: Intercourse introduces fresh fungal spores into the vaginal vault
options.C: Seminal fluid stimulates excess production of protective lactobacilli
options.D: Friction causes physical trauma to the inflamed cervical tissue

explanation: The basic pH of semen vaporizes the volatile amines generated in bacterial vaginosis, making the fishy smell much more noticeable. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h4)

question: What is the first step a nurse should anticipate during a physical assessment for suspected vaginitis?

options.A: Administering a broad-spectrum antifungal suppository immediately
options.B: Inserting an indwelling urinary catheter to check for retention
options.C: Obtaining a complete blood count via venipuncture
options.D: Inspecting the external genitalia for erythema and abnormal discharge

explanation: Visual inspection of the external structures provides immediate clues about inflammation before performing internal speculum exams. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h5)

question: Which diagnostic tool is commonly used at the bedside to check the acidity of vaginal secretions?

options.A: pH indicator paper
options.B: A wooden tongue depressor
options.C: A standard glass thermometer
options.D: A sterile sphygmomanometer

explanation: Vaginal pH paper is a quick bedside test that helps differentiate between bacterial vaginosis, candidiasis, and trichomoniasis. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h5)

question: A patient is prescribed metronidazole for trichomoniasis. What critical instruction must the nurse include in her teaching?

options.A: Stop taking the medication as soon as itching goes away
options.B: Double the dose if a single daily pill is missed
options.C: Use petroleum jelly as a lubricant with the oral tablets
options.D: Avoid consuming alcohol during and immediately after treatment

explanation: Metronidazole causes a severe disulfiram-like reaction when mixed with alcohol, leading to severe nausea, vomiting, and headaches. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h6)

question: Why is it important for patients to complete the entire course of anti-infective therapy even if symptoms disappear?

options.A: To stimulate the long-term production of estrogen
options.B: To eradicate the pathogen completely and prevent recurrent infection
options.C: To prevent the development of systemic hypertension
options.D: To ensure the vaginal pH remains permanently alkaline

explanation: Stopping medication early leaves hardy microbes alive, which can quickly multiply and cause symptoms to return. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h6)

question: What is the term for the complete absence of the vagina at birth?

options.A: Septate vagina
options.B: Vaginal agenesis
options.C: Vaginal atresia
options.D: Hematocolpos

explanation: Vaginal agenesis refers to the congenital absence of all or part of the vagina resulting from abnormal embryonic development. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T11#GNS216_U5_T11_h1)

question: A young female patient with a transverse vaginal septum most likely presents with which clinical finding?

options.A: Continuous painless urinary incontinence
options.B: Complete absence of secondary sex characteristics
options.C: Recurrent severe pelvic inflammatory disease
options.D: Primary amenorrhea with pelvic pain

explanation: An obstructed vagina traps menstrual blood, causing cyclic pelvic pain and failure to menstruate despite normal hormonal development. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T11#GNS216_U5_T11_h1)

question: Herniation of the bladder into the anterior vaginal wall is known as what?

options.A: Enterocele
options.B: Urethrocele
options.C: Rectocele
options.D: Cystocele

explanation: A cystocele occurs when supporting tissues between a woman's bladder and vaginal wall weaken, allowing the bladder to drop into the vagina. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T11#GNS216_U5_T11_h2)

question: Obstetric fistulas involving the vagina are most commonly caused by what factor?

options.A: Prolonged and obstructed labor
options.B: Congenital malformation of Müllerian ducts
options.C: Severe untreated bacterial vaginosis
options.D: Incomplete surgical closure of an episiotomy

explanation: Pressures from prolonged obstructed labor cause ischemic necrosis of tissue between the vagina and surrounding organs, creating a fistula. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T11#GNS216_U5_T11_h2)

question: Which infection presents with a thick, white, cottage-like discharge and intense itching?

options.A: Vulvovaginal candidiasis
options.B: Trichomoniasis
options.C: Bacterial vaginosis
options.D: Atrophic vaginitis

explanation: Candida overgrowth produces characteristic pruritus and thick white discharge due to localized fungal inflammation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T11#GNS216_U5_T11_h3)

question: Why does atrophic vaginitis occur in postmenopausal women?

options.A: Increased glycogen production promotes unchecked bacterial colonization.
options.B: Declining estrogen levels lead to thinning and drying of the vaginal epithelium.
options.C: Loss of ovarian function stops the natural production of protective mucus.
options.D: Frequent hormonal fluctuations cause chronic hypertrophy of the mucosa.

explanation: Estrogen maintains the thickness, elasticity, and acidity of the vaginal lining; its drop during menopause causes atrophy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T11#GNS216_U5_T11_h3)

question: What diagnostic method is used to trace suspected vaginal fistulas using dye?

options.A: Methylene blue dye test
options.B: Bimanual pelvic palpation
options.C: Wet mount microscopy
options.D: Nucleic acid amplification test

explanation: Instilling dye into the bladder or rectum helps visualize leakage into the vagina, confirming the presence of a fistula tract. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T11#GNS216_U5_T11_h4)

question: A pelvic ultrasound is most useful when assessing which type of vaginal abnormality?

options.A: Microbial overgrowth in bacterial vaginosis
options.B: Hematocolpos due to an obstructed septum
options.C: Mild epithelial thinning in atrophic vaginitis
options.D: Surface mucosal inflammation from candidiasis

explanation: Ultrasound visualizes fluid collections within the reproductive tract caused by anatomical obstructions like an imperforate hymen or septum. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T11#GNS216_U5_T11_h4)

question: What is the primary medical treatment for bacterial vaginosis?

options.A: Acyclovir
options.B: Fluconazole
options.C: Metronidazole
options.D: Topical estrogen

explanation: Metronidazole is an antimicrobial agent effective against the anaerobic bacteria associated with bacterial vaginosis. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T11#GNS216_U5_T11_h5)

question: A patient with mild uterine and anterior vaginal wall prolapse declines immediate surgery. What is the most appropriate conservative nursing recommendation?

options.A: Regular vaginal douches with antiseptic solutions
options.B: Pelvic floor muscle exercises and pessary fitting
options.C: Prolonged bed rest with continuous catheterization
options.D: Daily systemic estrogen replacement therapy

explanation: Conservative management for mild prolapse includes pelvic floor strengthening and mechanical support using a pessary. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T11#GNS216_U5_T11_h5)

question: Why should nurses advise women against routine vaginal douching?

options.A: It causes immediate permanent closure of the vaginal canal.
options.B: It triggers severe allergic reactions in the pelvic muscles.
options.C: It prevents the absorption of necessary systemic hormones.
options.D: It washes away protective normal flora and disrupts the natural acidic pH.

explanation: Douching alters the delicate vaginal ecosystem, killing beneficial bacteria and predisposing the patient to infections. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T11#GNS216_U5_T11_h6)

question: What is a key nursing responsibility following reconstructive vaginal surgery?

options.A: Monitoring for signs of bleeding and infection
options.B: Encouraging early heavy lifting to test repair strength
options.C: Administering routine vaginal douches every shift
options.D: Removing urinary catheters immediately post-op

explanation: Postoperative monitoring focuses on detecting early complications such as hemorrhage or surgical site infection. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T11#GNS216_U5_T11_h6)

question: What anatomical structures are connected by a vesicovaginal fistula?

options.A: The bladder and the vagina
options.B: The ureter and the uterus
options.C: The urethra and the rectum
options.D: The kidney and the bladder

explanation: A vesicovaginal fistula forms an abnormal tract specifically between the urinary bladder and the vagina, causing continuous urine leakage. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h1)

question: The primary physical symptom experienced by a patient with a vesicovaginal fistula is...

options.A: Severe pain during bowel movements
options.B: Inability to pass urine at all
options.C: Continuous, involuntary leakage of urine
options.D: Bright red bleeding from the uterus

explanation: Because urine bypasses the urethral sphincter through the fistula tract, it leaks continuously into the vagina. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h1)

question: The leading cause of vesicovaginal fistula in Nigeria is...

options.A: Routine cesarean section
options.B: Bacterial urinary tract infections
options.C: Direct pelvic bone fractures
options.D: Prolonged obstructed labor

explanation: Prolonged and obstructed labor puts intense pressure on pelvic tissues, causing ischemia and fistula formation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h2)

question: How does prolonged labor directly damage the bladder and vaginal tissue?

options.A: By introducing aggressive bacterial toxins directly
options.B: By overstretching the bladder smooth muscle
options.C: By causing ischemia through sustained pressure
options.D: By dissolving the mucosal lining with amniotic fluid

explanation: Pressure from the fetal head cuts off blood supply to the tissues, leading to tissue death and fistula creation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h2)

question: When does urinary leakage typically begin after childbirth in a patient developing a VVF?

options.A: Only when the patient stands up suddenly
options.B: Several months after the menstrual cycle returns
options.C: Immediately during the second stage of labor
options.D: A few days postpartum as necrotic tissue sloughs

explanation: Dead tissue takes a few days to separate and slough off after ischemic injury, revealing the abnormal opening. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h3)

question: What is the purpose of instilling methylene blue dye during the evaluation of a suspected fistula?

options.A: To trace the leakage path and confirm the diagnosis
options.B: To stain the vaginal mucosa for a biopsy sample
options.C: To numb the bladder lining and reduce patient discomfort
options.D: To sterilize the bladder walls before surgical repair

explanation: The blue dye passes through the fistula opening, staining vaginal packing to visually confirm the tract. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h3)

question: A major skin integrity risk for patients with a vesicovaginal fistula is...

options.A: Ammoniacal dermatitis and vulvar excoriation
options.B: Diffuse fungal infections of the scalp
options.C: Pressure ulcers over the shoulder blades
options.D: Hyperpigmentation of the lower extremities

explanation: Constant exposure of the perineal skin to urine causes severe irritation, breakdown, and excoriation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h4)

question: Why is nutritional assessment particularly important prior to fistula repair surgery?

options.A: To promote optimal wound healing and tissue recovery
options.B: To eliminate the need for post-operative antibiotics
options.C: To stop the continuous involuntary flow of urine
options.D: To prevent the development of gestational diabetes

explanation: Good nutrition and correction of anemia are essential for proper tissue healing and successful surgical closure. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h4)

question: The primary goal of bladder catheterization after a VVF repair is to...

options.A: Flush out remaining methylene blue diagnostic dye
options.B: Measure the exact concentration of urinary protein
options.C: Keep the bladder continuously empty and tension-free
options.D: Deliver topical medications directly to the suture line

explanation: Continuous drainage prevents bladder distension, which would otherwise pull apart the fresh surgical sutures. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h5)

question: Why is encouraging a high fluid intake important during the post-operative recovery period?

options.A: To dilute the concentration of prescribed pain medications
options.B: To speed up the reabsorption of suture materials
options.C: To shrink the overall size of the urinary bladder
options.D: To prevent catheter blockage and maintain urinary flow

explanation: Good hydration flushes the catheter lumen and prevents clots or debris from blocking urine drainage. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h5)

question: A comprehensive recovery plan for a VVF survivor must include...

options.A: Immediate discharge home without follow-up care
options.B: Strict limitation of fluid intake for several months
options.C: Psychological support and social reintegration activities
options.D: Permanent prohibition from ever becoming pregnant again

explanation: Patients suffer severe emotional trauma, stigma, and isolation, making psychosocial rehabilitation a vital part of recovery. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h6)

question: Which strategy is most effective for preventing new cases of vesicovaginal fistula in Nigeria?

options.A: Increasing the availability of adult literacy classes
options.B: Distributing barrier contraceptives in rural markets
options.C: Providing timely access to emergency obstetric care
options.D: Administering prophylactic antibiotics to all pregnant women

explanation: Prompt intervention for obstructed labor prevents the prolonged tissue ischemia that causes fistula formation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T12#GNS216_U5_T12_h6)

question: What is a rectovaginal fistula?

options.A: A congenital narrowing of the lower vaginal canal
options.B: A tear in the perineal skin reaching the anus
options.C: An abnormal tract connecting the rectum and vagina
options.D: An infection of the Bartholin's gland in the vulva

explanation: A rectovaginal fistula creates an unwanted passage between the rectal wall and the vaginal wall, leading to the leakage of stool or gas through the vagina. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h1)

question: Why does a rectovaginal fistula cause psychological distress for patients?

options.A: Sudden and permanent loss of all lower limb mobility
options.B: Involuntary passage of flatus and feces through the vagina
options.C: Complete inability to ever conceive biological children again
options.D: Severe chronic pain located exclusively in the upper abdomen

explanation: The uncontrolled leakage of bowel contents via the vaginal opening causes profound hygiene challenges and social embarrassment. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h1)

question: The primary cause of rectovaginal fistulas in Nigeria is:

options.A: Chronic pelvic inflammatory disease caused by STIs
options.B: Obstetric trauma from prolonged obstructed labor
options.C: Congenital malformations present from early childhood
options.D: Routine use of midline episiotomies by midwives

explanation: Unrelieved obstructed labor compresses the vaginal and rectal tissues, leading to tissue death and subsequent fistula formation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h2)

question: How does ischemia contribute to fistula formation during difficult labor?

options.A: Infected amniotic fluid eats away at the vaginal mucosa
options.B: Hormonal imbalances prevent normal postpartum tissue healing
options.C: Compressed blood supply causes localized tissue death and breakdown
options.D: Extreme physical stretching instantly tears the muscle fibers apart

explanation: Pressure from the baby's head cuts off oxygen supply to the septum, resulting in necrosis and an opening between the organs. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h2)

question: What is the classic symptom reported by a patient with a rectovaginal fistula?

options.A: Passage of feces and flatus through the vagina
options.B: Bright red bleeding from the urethra during urination
options.C: Severe sharp pain during the start of menstruation
options.D: Inability to control the flow of urine while coughing

explanation: The defining clinical feature is the escape of bowel contents through the vaginal canal due to the abnormal tract. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h3)

question: A patient complains of recurrent foul-smelling vaginal discharge and passing gas vaginally after a difficult delivery. What condition should you suspect first?

options.A: Rectovaginal fistula
options.B: Cervical polyp
options.C: Bartholin cyst
options.D: Uterine prolapse

explanation: These classic symptoms point directly to an abnormal connection between the bowel and the reproductive tract following childbirth. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h3)

question: What bedside test uses a colored dye in the rectum to confirm a rectovaginal fistula?

options.A: Litmus paper acidity test
options.B: Potassium hydroxide test
options.C: Normal saline wash test
options.D: Methylene blue dye test

explanation: Instilling methylene blue into the rectum and checking for blue stains on a vaginal gauze confirms the presence of a tract. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h4)

question: Why is an examination under anesthesia (EUA) often performed before scheduling fistula surgery?

options.A: To clean out impacted stool from the large intestine prior to surgery
options.B: To immediately close the opening while the patient is fully unconscious
options.C: To prevent the development of a postoperative wound infection
options.D: To accurately assess tissue quality and exact fistula location without patient pain

explanation: Relaxed pelvic muscles under anesthesia allow the clinician to thoroughly evaluate the defect and plan the appropriate surgical approach. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h4)

question: The primary goal of bowel preparation before rectovaginal fistula surgery is to:

options.A: Prevent the formation of deep vein thrombosis
options.B: Stimulate rapid weight gain before the operation
options.C: Minimize fecal contamination of the surgical site
options.D: Diagnose the exact cause of the original tear

explanation: Clearing the bowel reduces stool load and lowers the risk of wound infection and repair breakdown. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h5)

question: Why is nutritional optimization a key component of preoperative care for these patients?

options.A: High-fiber diets eliminate the need for mechanical enemas
options.B: Full nutrient stores prevent the need for general anesthesia
options.C: Good nutrition stops the fistula tract from growing larger
options.D: Adequate protein and vitamins promote optimal wound healing

explanation: Surgical repair of ischemic or damaged tissue requires proper cellular nutrition to ensure the tissues successfully knit together. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h5)

question: When is a temporary colostomy most likely created during rectovaginal fistula management?

options.A: For every single routine primary transvaginal repair
options.B: As a permanent replacement for normal bowel function
options.C: Only when the patient refuses to take oral antibiotics
options.D: In complex, recurrent, or badly damaged fistula cases

explanation: Diverting stool protects delicate or complicated surgical repairs from fecal contamination while healing takes place. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of using a tissue flap during a rectovaginal fistula repair?

options.A: To permanently block the normal passage of urine
options.B: To stretch the vaginal canal to a larger diameter
options.C: To cover the defect with well-vascularized, healthy tissue
options.D: To completely eliminate the need for postoperative antibiotics

explanation: Bringing fresh, good-blood-supply tissue over the repaired area greatly improves the chances of successful tissue fusion. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h6)

question: Why are stool softeners commonly prescribed after rectovaginal fistula repair?

options.A: To completely stop bowel function for several weeks
options.B: To speed up the total digestion time of all food eaten
options.C: To cure any lingering urinary tract infections quickly
options.D: To prevent straining and protect the suture line from pressure

explanation: Soft stools pass easily without requiring hard pushing, which prevents the fresh stitches from tearing apart. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h7)

question: What is a key nursing intervention regarding bladder management post-surgery?

options.A: Removing all fluid intake to keep the surgical dressings dry
options.B: Checking urine specific gravity every thirty minutes around the clock
options.C: Maintaining an indwelling urinary catheter to prevent bladder distension
options.D: Encouraging heavy physical exercise to stimulate normal voiding reflexes

explanation: A distended bladder pushes against the anterior vaginal wall, placing unwanted mechanical stress on the healing surgical repair. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h7)

question: The most common and challenging complication after a rectovaginal fistula repair is:

options.A: Permanent total paralysis of both lower limbs
options.B: Complete loss of kidney function requiring dialysis
options.C: Sudden spontaneous rupture of the uterine wall
options.D: Fistula recurrence and failure of the repair

explanation: Due to tension, infection, or poor tissue quality, some repairs fail to heal, resulting in the return of the fistula tract. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h8)

question: What can cause vaginal or rectal strictures following fistula surgery?

options.A: Excessive scar tissue formation during the healing process
options.B: Consuming a high-fiber diet too early in recovery
options.C: Failure to administer high doses of intravenous fluids
options.D: Leaving the indwelling urinary catheter in place too long

explanation: Fibrous scar tissue can contract and narrow the lumen of the vagina or rectum, leading to strictures. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h8)

question: What primary part of the female reproductive tract is affected by cervicitis?

options.A: The fallopian tubes
options.B: The uterine cervix
options.C: The ovarian cortex
options.D: The myometrium wall

explanation: Cervicitis specifically refers to inflammation localized to the cervix of the uterus. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h1)

question: How is chronic cervicitis best told apart from acute cervicitis?

options.A: Exclusive presence of viral pathogens
options.B: Sudden and severe purulent vaginal discharge
options.C: A long-standing inflammatory cellular infiltrate
options.D: Immediate response to single-dose antibiotic therapy

explanation: Chronic cervicitis features persistent infiltration of lymphocytes and plasma cells rather than sudden purulent discharge. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h1)

question: Neisseria gonorrhoeae is classified under which microbiological category?

options.A: Flagellated protozoan
options.B: Obligate intracellular virus
options.C: Gram-negative diplococcus
options.D: Gram-positive bacillus

explanation: Neisseria gonorrhoeae is a gram-negative diplococcus bacterium known for causing purulent infections. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h2)

question: A patient with cervicitis reports regular use of chemical contraceptive sponges and spermicides without any STIs. What kind of cause does this point to?

options.A: Protozoan infestation
options.B: Non-infectious chemical irritation
options.C: Endogenous fungal overgrowth
options.D: Obligate viral infection

explanation: Exposure to spermicides and barrier devices can trigger localized inflammatory reactions without a microbial pathogen. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h2)

question: What main tissue change causes bleeding after sex in someone with cervicitis?

options.A: Atrophy of the vaginal rugae
options.B: Friable and hyperemic cervical tissue
options.C: Obstruction of the cervical os
options.D: Hypertrophy of the myometrium

explanation: Inflammation makes the cervical blood vessels congested and fragile, leading to bleeding upon mechanical contact during intercourse. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h3)

question: Why do many women with Chlamydia-induced cervicitis remain undiagnosed for a long time?

options.A: The pathogen only affects the outer squamous epithelium
options.B: Routine diagnostic tests cannot detect intracellular bacteria
options.C: The infection frequently presents with minimal or absent symptoms
options.D: Symptoms only appear after menopause occurs

explanation: Chlamydial cervicitis is notoriously subtle, causing few noticeable symptoms and delaying healthcare-seeking behavior. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h3)

question: What is recognized as the gold standard laboratory test for detecting Chlamydia trachomatis?

options.A: Urinary dipstick for protein
options.B: Cervical biopsy for histology
options.C: Complete blood cell count
options.D: Nucleic Acid Amplification Test

explanation: Nucleic Acid Amplification Tests provide high sensitivity and specificity for identifying bacterial genetic material. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h4)

question: During a speculum examination for suspected cervicitis, what physical sign should the nurse expect to see?

options.A: A closed, pale, and completely dry external os
options.B: Mucopurulent discharge and cervical friability
options.C: Hypertrophic fibroid tissue protruding outward
options.D: Extensive ulceration of the labia majora

question: Confirmed gonococcal cervicitis is typically treated with which main antibiotic?

options.A: Ceftriaxone
options.B: Penicillin G
options.C: Fluconazole
options.D: Vancomycin

explanation: Ceftriaxone is the cornerstone antibiotic recommended for treating Neisseria gonorrhoeae infections. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h5)

question: Why is treating sexual partners at the same time essential in infectious cervicitis?

options.A: To enhance the systemic absorption of oral antibiotics
options.B: To prevent reinfection of the patient through untreated partners
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of community screening programs
options.D: To eliminate the requirement for follow-up pelvic examinations

explanation: Treating partners stops the cycle of transmission, ensuring the patient is not immediately reinfected after finishing medication. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h5)

question: What serious upper reproductive tract complication can happen if lower cervicitis is left untreated?

options.A: Ovarian follicular cysts
options.B: Endometrial hyperplasia
options.C: Pelvic inflammatory disease
options.D: Vaginal wall prolapse

question: A patient treated for chlamydial cervicitis asks when she can safely have sex again. What should the nurse advise?

options.A: Use hormonal contraceptives instead of barrier methods during healing

question: What is the primary physical characteristic of cervical polyps?

options.A: Hard and immovable bony lumps
options.B: Fluid-filled blister lesions
options.C: Rough and scaly patches
options.D: Soft and fragile finger-like growths

question: Why must removed cervical polyps be sent to the laboratory for examination?

options.A: To measure exact hormone levels
options.B: To test for active bacterial infections
options.C: To check for abnormal cancerous changes
options.D: To determine the patient's blood type

explanation: Although most polyps are non-cancerous, microscopic analysis is necessary to rule out rare malignant changes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h1)

question: Which part of the inner cervix is typically lined by columnar epithelium where polyps often start?

options.A: Endocervix
options.B: Ectocervix
options.C: Vaginal fornix
options.D: Squamous junction

explanation: The endocervical canal is lined by columnar epithelium, which is the common site for polyp origin. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h2)

question: Which hormone plays the main role in stimulating the growth of cervical polyps?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Cortisol

explanation: Estrogen stimulation promotes the localized overgrowth of cervical tissue. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h2)

question: Which group of women is most frequently affected by cervical polyps?

options.A: Postmenopausal males
options.B: Young girls before puberty
options.C: Women of reproductive age
options.D: Elderly women who have never given birth

explanation: Cervical polyps are most commonly found in women who are menstruating and in perimenopausal women. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h3)

question: How does chronic inflammation of the cervix contribute to polyp formation?

options.A: By destroying the surface skin cells
options.B: By blocking the urinary tubes
options.C: By depleting the body's immune system
options.D: By causing ongoing tissue irritation and cell overgrowth

question: A patient with a cervical polyp commonly presents with which symptom?

options.A: Postcoital bleeding
options.B: Upper abdominal cramping
options.C: Involuntary urine leakage
options.D: Severe lower back pain

explanation: Friction during sexual intercourse easily disrupts the fragile blood vessels of a polyp, causing bleeding. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h4)

question: Why do cervical polyps often cause abnormal vaginal discharge?

options.A: Dead polyp tissue turns into thick pus
options.B: The growths block normal urine flow from the bladder
options.C: The ongoing irritation causes excess mucus production
options.D: Polyps constantly secrete large amounts of plain water

explanation: Inflammation and stimulation of the glands by the polyp lead to increased mucus discharge. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h4)

question: Which instrument is used to examine the cervix closely under magnification?

options.A: Laryngoscope
options.B: Stethoscope
options.C: Colposcope
options.D: Ophthalmoscope

explanation: A colposcope provides a magnified view of the cervix to help healthcare providers evaluate abnormal tissues. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h5)

question: A patient scheduled for a cervical polyp removal expresses fear of cancer. What is the nurse's best response?

options.A: The doctor would have known immediately without a biopsy.
options.B: You only need to worry if the bleeding gets much heavier.
options.C: Do not worry because cancer never happens in young women.
options.D: Most polyps are benign, but removal and biopsy are done to confirm.

explanation: This response provides accurate reassurance while validating the necessity of histological confirmation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h5)

question: What is the standard clinic procedure for removing a small cervical polyp?

options.A: Surgically removing the entire uterus
options.B: Applying strong acid drops to dissolve it
options.C: Twisting it off gently at the base with forceps
options.D: Freezing the entire cervix with liquid nitrogen

question: Why is the base of the polyp often treated with heat or chemical cautery after removal?

options.A: To kill any fungi in the vagina
options.B: To stop bleeding and prevent the polyp from growing back
options.C: To numb the local nerve endings completely
options.D: To widen the cervical canal to improve fertility

explanation: Cauterization controls bleeding and destroys any remaining tissue cells at the root. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h6)

question: Which activity should a patient avoid immediately after having a cervical polyp removed?

options.A: Drinking warm fluids
options.B: Taking prescribed oral vitamins
options.C: Walking short distances
options.D: Using vaginal tampons

explanation: Tampons should be avoided after the procedure to prevent infection and give the cervix time to heal. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h7)

question: A patient calls the clinic reporting light spotting two days after a polypectomy. What is the appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Tell her to stop all prescribed pain medications right away
options.B: Advise her to come in immediately for an emergency blood transfusion
options.C: Instruct her to douche with antiseptic solution immediately
options.D: Reassure her that mild spotting is expected during the healing process

explanation: Light spotting and mild cramping are normal temporary findings following a cervical polypectomy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T15#GNS216_U5_T15_h7)

question: What part of the female reproductive system does cervical irritation affect?

options.A: The muscular upper body of the uterus
options.B: The glandular tissue inside the ovaries
options.C: The inner lining of the fallopian tubes
options.D: The lower fibromuscular portion of the uterus

explanation: The cervix is the lower, cylindrical portion of the uterus that connects to the vagina, making it the primary site for this condition. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h1)

question: A patient reports spotting after sexual intercourse. How is this symptom clinically described?

options.A: Retrograde menstruation
options.B: Contact bleeding
options.C: Cryptomenorrhea
options.D: Menorrhagia

explanation: Bleeding that occurs immediately after sexual activity is termed contact bleeding or post-coital spotting, a classic sign of cervical irritation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h1)

question: Which epithelial type lines the endocervical canal?

options.A: Keratinized stratified squamous epithelium
options.B: Non-keratinized stratified squamous epithelium
options.C: Mucus-secreting columnar epithelium
options.D: Simple ciliated cuboidal epithelium

explanation: The endocervix is lined by a single layer of columnar cells that produce protective cervical mucus. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h2)

question: Why is the transformation zone clinically significant in cervical health?

options.A: It acts as a complete physical barrier against all viral infections
options.B: It is where most cervical cellular changes and pathologies occur
options.C: It produces the primary hormones required for monthly ovulation
options.D: It stores mature ova prior to the fertilization process

explanation: The continuous cellular remodeling at the squamocolumnar junction makes this transformation zone prone to abnormal changes and infections. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common infectious cause of cervical irritation?

options.A: Neisseria gonorrhoeae via sexual contact
options.B: Escherichia coli via the bloodstream
options.C: Human Papillomavirus via skin contact
options.D: Chlamydia trachomatis via sexual transmission

explanation: While E. coli causes urinary tract infections, STIs like Chlamydia, Gonorrhea, and HPV are the primary infectious drivers of cervical irritation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h3)

question: A patient who regularly uses scented vaginal douches presents with vaginal soreness and discharge. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Chemical contact irritation
options.B: Endometrial hyperplasia
options.C: Ovarian cyst rupture
options.D: Ectopic tubal pregnancy

explanation: Scented douches disrupt the normal vaginal flora and expose delicate cervical and vaginal tissues to harsh chemicals, causing contact irritation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h3)

question: What physiological change causes the cervix to bleed easily during an examination?

options.A: Mucosal friability resulting from inflammation
options.B: Complete atrophy of the underlying muscular wall
options.C: Rapid calcification of the transformation zone
options.D: Obstruction of the main internal os

explanation: Inflammation weakens the tissue and increases blood vessel fragility, creating mucosal friability that bleeds on contact. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h4)

question: What is the medical term for pain experienced during sexual intercourse?

options.A: Dysmenorrhea
options.B: Dysuria
options.C: Dyspareunia
options.D: Dyspareflexia

explanation: Dyspareunia is the term used to describe painful sexual intercourse, often resulting from inflamed or irritated pelvic structures. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of collecting a cervical swab during a diagnostic evaluation?

options.A: To determine the patient's exact hormonal ovulation phase
options.B: To measure systemic blood glucose and electrolyte levels
options.C: To identify specific infectious organisms via culture or PCR
options.D: To surgically remove abnormal cells from the transformation zone

explanation: Cervical swabs isolate pathogens responsible for inflammation, guiding precise antimicrobial therapy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h5)

question: A nurse is preparing a patient for a speculum examination to investigate cervical irritation. What is the most appropriate action?

options.A: Administer general anesthesia before inserting the vaginal speculum
options.B: Place the patient in a prone position with a pillow under the hips
options.C: Explain the procedure and place the patient in the lithotomy position
options.D: Instruct the patient to empty her bowel using an oral laxative first

explanation: Clear explanation reduces anxiety, and the lithotomy position provides optimal exposure for viewing the cervix. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h5)

question: Why is pelvic rest often recommended during the active treatment of cervical irritation?

options.A: To increase systemic absorption of oral antibiotic medications
options.B: To completely halt the normal monthly menstrual cycle temporarily
options.C: To prevent mechanical trauma and allow the inflamed mucosa to heal
options.D: To prevent the development of secondary urinary tract infections

explanation: Avoiding sexual intercourse and tampons stops mechanical friction, giving delicate cervical tissues time to recover. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h6)

question: Which intervention is standard when cervical irritation stems from a confirmed bacterial infection?

options.A: Targeted antibiotic therapy
options.B: Immediate radiation therapy
options.C: Surgical excision of the cervix
options.D: High-dose systemic corticosteroid pills

explanation: Bacterial infections require specific antimicrobial agents to eradicate the causative pathogen and resolve the inflammatory process. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h6)

question: What is the main reason nurses advise against routine vaginal douching?

options.A: It disrupts the protective vaginal flora and pushes pathogens upward
options.B: It permanently alters the anatomical structure of the uterine cervix
options.C: It causes immediate and irreversible closure of the endocervical os
options.D: It prevents the normal absorption of systemic oral contraceptives

explanation: Douching washes away beneficial bacteria that maintain acidic protection, making the reproductive tract vulnerable to ascending infections. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h7)

question: Which screening tool is primarily used to detect early pre-cancerous cellular changes on the cervix?

options.A: Complete blood count
options.B: Pelvic ultrasound scan
options.C: Pap smear test
options.D: Urinalysis dipstick test

explanation: The Papanicolaou (Pap) smear examines exfoliated cervical cells under a microscope to detect dysplasia and early cellular abnormalities. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h7)

question: What is the proper medical term for cervical erosion?

options.A: Atrophic vaginitis
options.B: Cervical dysplasia
options.C: Cervical ectropion
options.D: Endometrial hyperplasia

explanation: Cervical ectropion is the correct clinical term for cervical erosion because it describes the outward turning of the endocervical lining. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h1)

question: Why is the term 'erosion' misleading when describing this condition?

options.A: There is no actual wearing away or ulceration of the tissue
options.B: The lesion only appears on the outer surface of the vagina
options.C: The tissue is actually thickening instead of shedding
options.D: The red appearance is caused by active bacterial infection

explanation: The condition involves a displacement of cells rather than a physical breakdown or ulceration of the mucosal surface. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h1)

question: What type of tissue normally covers the ectocervix?

options.A: Columnar epithelium
options.B: Ciliated simple epithelium
options.C: Stratified squamous epithelium
options.D: Transitional epithelium

explanation: The ectocervix is covered by protective stratified squamous epithelium that withstands the physical environment of the vagina. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h2)

question: Where is the squamocolumnar junction located?

options.A: At the meeting point of the ectocervix and endocervix
options.B: At the superior opening leading into the uterine cavity
options.C: Along the lateral walls of the upper vaginal vault
options.D: Deep within the muscular wall of the myometrium

explanation: The squamocolumnar junction marks the dynamic border where the squamous cells of the outer cervix meet the columnar cells of the inner canal. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h2)

question: Which hormone is the primary driver of cervical ectropion development?

options.A: Prolactin
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Progesterone
options.D: Estrogen

explanation: High levels of estrogen stimulate the growth and outward movement of the columnar cells lining the endocervix. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h3)

question: How do hormonal contraceptives cause cervical ectropion?

options.A: Contraceptives cause direct mechanical trauma to the outer os
options.B: Synthetic hormones mimic estrogen and stimulate columnar cell migration
options.C: Progesterone levels drop and cause rapid shedding of squamous cells
options.D: Synthetic hormones trigger an inflammatory response in the stroma

explanation: Exogenous hormones in oral contraceptives raise estrogenic activity, leading to the eversion of the endocervical epithelium. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h3)

question: What are Nabothian cysts?

options.A: Infected abscesses caused by bacterial invasion of the stroma
options.B: Malignant tumors developing from chronic cervical inflammation
options.C: Fluid-filled blisters resulting from herpes simplex virus infections
options.D: Mucus-filled retention cysts formed when squamous cells block gland ducts

explanation: Nabothian cysts develop when new metaplastic squamous epithelium covers and obstructs the openings of endocervical glands. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h4)

question: What cellular process transforms exposed columnar epithelium back into squamous epithelium?

options.A: Squamous metaplasia
options.B: Atrophic involution
options.C: Necrotic degeneration
options.D: Cellular hypertrophy

explanation: Squamous metaplasia is the adaptive replacement process where reserve cells generate new squamous epithelium to protect the exposed cervix. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h4)

question: What is the most common symptom reported by women with symptomatic cervical ectropion?

options.A: Foul-smelling green discharge with intense itching
options.B: Postcoital bleeding and excess mucus discharge
options.C: Severe lower abdominal cramping and high fever
options.D: Complete cessation of regular menstrual periods

explanation: The fragile, highly vascular columnar cells bleed easily upon contact and secrete excess mucus, leading to discharge and spotting. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h5)

question: Why do patients with cervical ectropion frequently experience postcoital bleeding?

options.A: The deep myometrial layers are weakened by hormonal fluctuations
options.B: Infection destroys the structural integrity of the vaginal walls
options.C: The exposed columnar epithelium has delicate capillaries that tear easily
options.D: Prolonged estrogen exposure causes ulceration of the cervix

explanation: Columnar cells on the ectocervix are fragile and lack the thick protective layers of squamous cells, making superficial capillaries vulnerable to friction. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h5)

question: Which diagnostic tool provides magnified visualization of the cervix during assessment?

options.A: Hysteroscope
options.B: Colposcope
options.C: Laparoscope
options.D: Otoscope

explanation: A colposcope is used to examine the cervix under magnification, helping differentiate benign ectropion from dysplasia. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h6)

question: What is the primary reason for performing a Pap smear when cervical ectropion is suspected?

options.A: To definitively cure the underlying tissue displacement
options.B: To culture active bacterial growth in the canal
options.C: To rule out abnormal cell changes or malignancy
options.D: To measure circulating levels of reproductive hormones

explanation: Cytology screening is essential because visual appearance alone cannot reliably distinguish benign ectropion from pre-cancerous lesions. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h6)

question: What is the appropriate initial management for an asymptomatic patient with cervical ectropion?

options.A: Reassurance and routine clinical observation
options.B: Aggressive systemic antibiotic therapy
options.C: Cauterization of the transformation zone
options.D: Immediate surgical removal of the entire cervix

explanation: Since benign ectropion without symptoms requires no treatment, reassurance and monitoring are standard practice. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h7)

question: Why might a clinician change a patient's oral contraceptive method to manage symptomatic ectropion?

options.A: To reduce exogenous estrogen levels driving the tissue eversion
options.B: To prevent the formation of permanent malignant tumors
options.C: To accelerate the natural shedding of the myometrium
options.D: To eliminate bacterial pathogens hiding inside the uterine cavity

explanation: Switching or stopping estrogen-containing contraceptives helps decrease the hormonal stimulation causing columnar cell overgrowth. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h7)

question: Which condition must always be ruled out when evaluating a patient with visible cervical redness and bleeding?

options.A: Cervical cancer or dysplasia
options.B: Polycystic ovary syndrome
options.C: Uterine fibroid degeneration
options.D: Endometriosis of the bladder

explanation: Malignancy and pre-cancerous cellular changes share visual similarities with ectropion and must be excluded through screening. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h8)

question: Why is distinguishing cervical ectropion from acute cervicitis important?

options.A: Infection makes the visual inspection of the transformation zone impossible
options.B: Ectropion prevents the transmission of sexually transmitted pathogens
options.C: Cervicitis requires specific antimicrobial treatment for infection, whereas simple ectropion does not
options.D: Cervicitis always progresses to malignant carcinoma if left untreated

explanation: Accurate diagnosis ensures that infectious causes receive appropriate antibiotic therapy rather than inappropriate surgical ablation. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T17#GNS216_U5_T17_h8)

question: Which virus is the main cause of cervical cancer?

options.A: Human Papillomavirus
options.B: Hepatitis B Virus
options.C: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.D: Herpes Simplex Virus

explanation: Persistent infection with high-risk strains of the Human Papillomavirus causes cellular changes that lead to cervical cancer. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h1)

question: Why is the transformation zone of the cervix most at risk for abnormal cell changes?
