explanation: The partograph uses a pictorial and graphic layout to display labour data clearly on a single sheet. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h1)

question: Why is the partograph considered an early warning system?

options.A: It predicts the exact hour of spontaneous delivery
options.B: It highlights deviations from normal labour progress early
options.C: It detects genetic abnormalities in the unborn baby
options.D: It measures the mother's baseline blood pressure accurately

explanation: Visual tracking helps nurses spot delayed progress or distress before severe complications happen. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h1)

question: An obstructed labour is best prevented by which benefit of the partograph?

options.A: Early detection of prolonged labour
options.B: Reduction of maternal nutritional needs
options.C: Lowering the cost of hospital admission
options.D: Accurate estimation of gestational age

explanation: Spotting delayed cervical dilation early stops labour from progressing into dangerous obstruction. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h2)

question: How does the partograph improve shift handovers among nurses?

options.A: By eliminating the need for verbal reports
options.B: By predicting the exact shift delivery numbers
options.C: By presenting standardized, clear visual data
options.D: By replacing the patient's bedside admission folder

explanation: A graphical layout allows incoming staff to assess the entire history of the labour at a quick glance. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h2)

question: How often should cervical dilation be plotted on the active phase partograph?

options.A: Every 2 hours
options.B: Once every shift
options.C: Every 30 minutes
options.D: Every 4 hours

explanation: Standard protocol requires cervical assessment and plotting every four hours during active labour. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h3)

question: Which parameter under maternal condition is monitored most frequently?

options.A: Pulse rate
options.B: Urine protein
options.C: Blood pressure
options.D: Body temperature

explanation: Maternal pulse is usually checked every thirty minutes to one hour, whereas blood pressure is checked every four hours. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h3)

question: What does a meconium-stained amniotic fluid recording usually indicate on the partograph?

options.A: Imminent maternal dehydration
options.B: Advanced maternal age
options.C: Foetal hypoxia or distress
options.D: Normal progression of the first stage

explanation: Passing meconium in utero typically signals that the foetus has experienced oxygen deprivation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h4)

question: When is the best time to count the foetal heart rate during labour?

options.A: During the peak of a strong contraction
options.B: Immediately after a uterine contraction
options.C: Only when the mother feels active kicks
options.D: Every 4 hours alongside cervical exams

explanation: Counting right after a contraction helps assess how the foetus recovers from the temporary drop in blood flow during the contraction. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h4)

question: What is the expected minimum rate of cervical dilation during active labour?

options.A: 1 cm per hour
options.B: 0.5 cm per hour
options.C: 3 cm per hour
options.D: 2 cm per hour

explanation: Normal active labour progresses at a minimum speed of 1 cm of cervical dilation every hour. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h5)

question: How are uterine contractions represented on the progress of labour grid?

options.A: By writing down numerical percentages
options.B: By drawing arrows pointing downwards
options.C: By shading grid squares based on duration
options.D: By charting maternal pain scores

explanation: Contraction length is visualized by shading boxes corresponding to how many seconds each contraction lasts. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h5)

question: How frequently should maternal blood pressure be recorded on a standard partograph?

options.A: Once every shift
options.B: Every 4 hours
options.C: Every hour
options.D: Every 30 minutes

explanation: Standard guidelines specify checking maternal blood pressure every four hours unless complications require tighter monitoring. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h6)

question: A rising maternal temperature logged every 4 hours on the partograph most likely points to what condition?

options.A: Rapid cervical dilation
options.B: Normal physiological exertion
options.C: Chorioamnionitis or infection
options.D: Severe foetal heart failure

explanation: Elevated temperature during prolonged labour often signals intrauterine infection, requiring prompt medical review. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h6)

question: At what cervical dilation does the alert line on the partograph begin?

options.A: 1 cm
options.B: 4 cm
options.C: 10 cm
options.D: 7 cm

explanation: The alert line marks the official onset of the active phase of labour, starting at 4 cm dilation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h7)

question: What action is required when the cervical dilation curve crosses the action line?

options.A: Discharging the patient home for rest
options.B: Stopping all intravenous fluid infusions
options.C: Waiting another four hours to observe progress
options.D: Immediate medical evaluation and definitive intervention

explanation: Crossing the action line means labour is severely delayed, requiring prompt clinical action like a Caesarean section or oxytocin. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h7)

question: When should entries be made on the partograph during labour?

options.A: When the doctor arrives for ward round
options.B: Only when abnormal symptoms appear
options.C: In real time as observations are made
options.D: From memory at the end of the shift

explanation: Immediate documentation prevents errors and ensures an accurate timeline of the labour process. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h8)

question: What is the primary responsibility of a nurse when a partograph shows abnormal trends?

options.A: Wait for the patient to request pain medication
options.B: Convert the partograph into a narrative case study
options.C: Hide the chart to prevent panic in the labour ward
options.D: Interpret the trends and initiate timely referrals or actions

explanation: Nurses must use the tool actively to catch delays early and trigger prompt multidisciplinary care. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T007#GNS226_U3_T007_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of the clean cloth inside a birth kit?

options.A: To clean the mother post-delivery
options.B: To bandage the umbilical stump
options.C: To line the delivery tray table
options.D: To dry and wrap the newborn

explanation: Drying the baby immediately prevents rapid heat loss and subsequent hypothermia in the neonate. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h1)

question: Why is a brand-new blade included in the clean birth kit?

options.A: To prevent tetanus and wound infections
options.B: To replace rusted hospital instruments
options.C: To measure the length of the cord
options.D: To ensure a fast and painless cut

explanation: A sterile, single-use blade prevents the introduction of Clostridium tetani spores into the umbilical stump. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h1)

question: A draft-free delivery room is primarily needed to protect against what condition?

options.A: Sudden uterine rupture
options.B: Hypothermia in the newborn
options.C: Maternal postpartum hemorrhage
options.D: Delayed placenta separation

explanation: Newborns lose body heat rapidly through convection when exposed to drafts in the delivery room. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h2)

question: A midwife preparing for an impending birth should check which emergency drug first?

options.A: Paracetamol
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Heparin
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Oxytocin must be immediately ready for active management of the third stage to prevent postpartum hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h2)

question: How often should the fetal heart rate be checked during the second stage of labour?

options.A: Every 5 minutes
options.B: Every 2 hours
options.C: Only after pushing starts
options.D: Every 30 minutes

explanation: The second stage carries higher risks of acute fetal distress, requiring very frequent heart rate checks. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h3)

question: What primary purpose does the partograph serve during active labour?

options.A: Determining the baby's exact gender
options.B: Scheduling the exact delivery time
options.C: Calculating hospital birth bills
options.D: Tracking maternal and fetal progress

explanation: The partograph provides a pictorial overview to spot prolonged labour and fetal distress early. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h3)

question: Which substance is unsafe to apply to the newborn umbilical cord stump?

options.A: Chlorhexidine gel
options.B: Mud or saliva
options.C: Dry gauze dressing
options.D: Clean air exposure

explanation: Unsterile substances like mud or saliva introduce harmful bacteria and tetanus spores directly into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h4)

question: What does the concept of the six cleans primarily aim to prevent?

options.A: Congenital malformations
options.B: Severe postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Prolonged second stage of labour
options.D: Puerperal and neonatal infections

explanation: The six cleans target infection routes to protect both the delivering mother and her newborn baby. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h4)

question: At what specific time intervals is the Apgar score routinely assessed?

options.A: 1 and 5 minutes
options.B: Immediately and 1 hour
options.C: 5 and 10 minutes
options.D: 10 and 20 minutes

explanation: Standard newborn assessment records Apgar scores at 1 minute to check tolerance and 5 minutes for extrauterine adaptation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h5)

question: A newborn with a heart rate of 90 beats per minute scores what value for the pulse sign?

options.A: 2 points
options.B: 1 point
options.C: 0 points
options.D: 3 points

explanation: A heart rate below 100 beats per minute earns 1 point, while a rate above 100 earns 2 points. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h5)

question: When should the uterotonic drug be administered during active management of the third stage?

options.A: Within one minute of birth
options.B: Before the baby's head crowns
options.C: Only after the placenta is out
options.D: After two hours of observation

explanation: Giving oxytocin within one minute ensures the drug peaks as the uterus empties, preventing uterine atony. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of performing uterine massage after placental delivery?

options.A: To speed up the healing of perineal tears
options.B: To encourage early initiation of breastfeeding
options.C: To stimulate myometrium contraction and stop bleeding
options.D: To help the mother pass trapped urine

explanation: Massage keeps the uterine muscles firmly contracted, compressing open blood vessels at the placental site. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h6)

question: What initial maneuver should a midwife perform when managing shoulder dystocia?

options.A: Immediate vacuum extraction
options.B: Internal podalic version
options.C: Fundal pressure
options.D: McRoberts maneuver

explanation: Hyperflexing the mother's legs toward her abdomen straightens the pelvis and dislodges the impacted shoulder. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h7)

question: A patient with a diagnosed umbilical cord prolapse should be placed in which position while awaiting theatre?

options.A: Upright sitting position
options.B: Left lateral position
options.C: Flat supine position
options.D: Knee-chest position

explanation: The knee-chest position uses gravity to keep the baby's weight off the prolapsed cord, preventing fetal hypoxia. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h7)

question: How often should maternal vital signs be checked during the first hour following delivery?

options.A: Every 15 minutes
options.B: Every 1 hour
options.C: Every 30 minutes
options.D: Only if she feels dizzy

explanation: The first hour post-delivery carries the highest risk for sudden hemorrhage, requiring checks every 15 minutes. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h8)

question: Why is monitoring bladder distension crucial in the immediate postnatal period?

options.A: It reduces the severity of perineal swelling
options.B: It helps the mother ambulate much faster
options.C: It prevents urinary tract infections permanently
options.D: A full bladder can cause uterine atony and bleeding

explanation: A distended bladder displaces the uterus, preventing effective contraction and increasing the risk of postpartum hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T008#GNS226_U3_T008_h8)

question: What is the main goal of Essential Obstetric Care in clinical practice?

options.A: Managing chronic non-communicable diseases in pregnancy
options.B: Reducing maternal and neonatal deaths from complications
options.C: Ensuring elective caesarean sections for all first-time mothers
options.D: Providing routine antenatal health education only

explanation: Essential Obstetric Care focuses specifically on treating life-threatening complications that happen during pregnancy, childbirth, and after delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h1)

question: Why is Essential Obstetric Care divided into basic and comprehensive levels?

options.A: To stop skilled birth attendants from performing deliveries
options.B: To separate antenatal care from postnatal care services
options.C: To determine the financial cost of hospital admissions
options.D: To match service delivery capabilities with facility resource levels

explanation: Dividing care ensures smaller clinics handle what they can safely manage while quickly referring complex cases to bigger hospitals. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h1)

question: How many specific medical functions must a health facility perform to be called a Basic Emergency Obstetric Care (BEmOC) center?

options.A: Seven functions
options.B: Four functions
options.C: Twelve functions
options.D: Nine functions

explanation: A health facility must be capable of executing all seven specific medical and obstetric interventions to be classified as a true BEmOC center. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h2)

question: Which procedure is a required duty for Basic Emergency Obstetric Care (BEmOC)?

options.A: Manual removal of a retained placenta
options.B: Conducting elective lower segment caesarean sections
options.C: Performing emergency exploratory laparotomy
options.D: Executing blood transfusion crossmatching procedures

explanation: Manual removal of the placenta and retained products of conception are core BEmOC responsibilities handled at primary health centers. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h2)

question: What two extra services make Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric Care (CEmOC) different from BEmOC facilities?

options.A: Antenatal ultrasound and routine vaccination
options.B: Neonatal resuscitation and oxytocin administration
options.C: Blood transfusion and emergency surgery
options.D: Manual vacuum aspiration and antibiotic therapy

explanation: Comprehensive care adds blood banking services and major surgeries like caesarean sections to the standard BEmOC list. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h3)

question: A woman in labor with a complete uterine rupture needs to be taken to a facility that offers which level of care?

options.A: Community-based traditional birth attendance
options.B: Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric Care
options.C: Basic Emergency Obstetric Care
options.D: Routine primary antenatal clinic care

explanation: Uterine rupture is a major surgical emergency that requires an immediate operation and blood transfusion, which are strictly CEmOC services. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h3)

question: How much blood loss defines primary postpartum hemorrhage after a normal vaginal delivery?

options.A: 1500 millilitres
options.B: 200 millilitres
options.C: 1000 millilitres
options.D: 500 millilitres

explanation: Primary postpartum hemorrhage is clinically defined as losing more than 500 mL of blood within the first twenty-four hours after childbirth. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h4)

question: A pregnant woman comes in with severe frontal headaches, blurred vision, and a blood pressure of 160/110 mmHg. What medication should the nurse-midwife prepare right away?

options.A: Magnesium sulphate
options.B: Ergometrine maleate
options.C: Oxytocin infusion
options.D: Methylergonovine

explanation: These signs point to severe pre-eclampsia, and magnesium sulphate is the drug used to prevent eclamptic fits. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h4)

question: What does crossing the alert line on a partograph mean during active labor?

options.A: The baby has suddenly entered severe distress
options.B: Cervical dilation has reached ten centimeters complete
options.C: Labor is moving slower than normal and needs close monitoring
options.D: The second stage of labor has safely finished

explanation: The alert line acts as an early warning that cervical dilation is falling behind the expected rate of one centimetre per hour. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h5)

question: A nurse-midwife checking a partograph sees that cervical dilation has crossed the action line. What is the correct action to take?

options.A: Wait another four hours to see if labor picks up on its own
options.B: Stop all monitoring and give oral sedatives
options.C: Start immediate treatment or transfer to a comprehensive facility
options.D: Send the patient home with instructions to return tomorrow

explanation: Crossing the action line means labor is delayed too long; prompt action like medical help or surgical delivery is required right away. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h5)

question: Why is it important to soak used metal instruments in a chlorine solution before washing them?

options.A: To kill bloodborne germs and protect the people handling them
options.B: To lubricate the joints on speculums and needle holders
options.C: To remove rust and polish the metal surfaces
options.D: To sharpen the blades of surgical scissors

explanation: Decontamination is an initial safety step that kills infectious agents like HIV and Hepatitis viruses before cleaning and sterilizing. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h6)

question: Which practice helps the most in preventing uterine infections in the labor ward?

options.A: Giving routine intravenous antibiotics to every patient
options.B: Stopping all family members from entering the delivery suite
options.C: Keeping unnecessary digital vaginal exams during labor to a minimum
options.D: Doing daily vaginal washes with antiseptic soaps

explanation: Limiting vaginal exams reduces the risk of pushing bacteria from the lower birth canal up into the sterile uterus. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h6)

question: In the 'three delays' model of maternal mortality, what does the second delay mean?

options.A: Delay in hospital staff starting surgery
options.B: Delay in reaching a health facility because of transport or distance
options.C: Delay in the family noticing a danger sign
options.D: Delay in the patient taking oral drugs at home

explanation: The second delay involves transport problems, bad roads, and long distances between communities and emergency clinics. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h7)

question: Before sending a patient with postpartum hemorrhage from a local clinic to a CEmOC hospital, what must the nurse-midwife do first?

options.A: Wait until the bleeding stops completely without medical help
options.B: Complete all financial billing paperwork before leaving
options.C: Stabilize vital signs and set up an intravenous (IV) line
options.D: Tell the patient to find her own transport

explanation: Stabilization, such as giving IV fluids and oxytocin, is necessary to keep the patient alive while traveling. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h7)

question: What happens to pulmonary vascular resistance when the newborn takes the first breath?

options.A: It remains completely unchanged
options.B: It drops drastically
options.C: It fluctuates randomly
options.D: It increases sharply

explanation: Filling the lungs with air expands the pulmonary vessels and lowers resistance to blood flow. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h1)

question: A failure in clearing fluid from the alveoli at birth primarily results in what condition?

options.A: Neonatal jaundice
options.B: Transient tachypnea only
options.C: Congenital heart failure
options.D: Persistent pulmonary hypertension

explanation: Retained fluid prevents normal oxygenation, causing blood vessels in the lungs to stay constricted. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h1)

question: How many initial screening questions are asked immediately after a baby is born?

options.A: Three
options.B: Six
options.C: Two
options.D: Four

explanation: The rapid initial evaluation relies on four questions covering gestation, fluid, breathing, and tone. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h2)

question: A newborn delivered through thick meconium-stained amniotic fluid requires what initial action if vigorous?

options.A: Immediate chest compressions
options.B: Routine endotracheal suctioning
options.C: Routine observation with the mother
options.D: Emergency umbilical catheterization

explanation: Vigorous infants with meconium staining do not need routine intubation and suctioning; they stay with the mother. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h2)

question: What is the primary reason for drying a newborn immediately after birth?

options.A: To prevent hypothermia
options.B: To stimulate crying
options.C: To remove vernix caseosa
options.D: To check for skin rashes

explanation: Wet skin combined with delivery room drafts causes rapid heat loss through evaporation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h3)

question: Delayed umbilical cord clamping for stable newborns primarily helps achieve which benefit?

options.A: Reduced risk of jaundice
options.B: Lower blood pressure
options.C: Improved iron stores
options.D: Faster meconium passage

explanation: Allowing blood to transfer from the placenta before clamping boosts the infant's blood volume and iron reserves. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h3)

question: Which part of the airway should be suctioned first when using a bulb syringe?

options.A: Nose
options.B: Mouth
options.C: Pharynx
options.D: Trachea

explanation: Suctioning the mouth before the nose prevents the infant from gasping and aspirating pooled oral secretions. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h4)

question: A newborn fails to breathe after initial drying and positioning. What is the next best action?

options.A: Administer epinephrine through an IV
options.B: Insert an endotracheal tube
options.C: Start chest compressions immediately
options.D: Provide gentle tactile stimulation

explanation: Tactile stimulation is the next step to prompt breathing before moving on to positive pressure ventilation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h4)

question: What is the heart rate threshold that indicates an immediate need for positive pressure ventilation?

options.A: Below 80 beats per minute
options.B: Below 140 beats per minute
options.C: Below 60 beats per minute
options.D: Below 100 beats per minute

explanation: A heart rate under 100 beats per minute indicates inadequate breathing and requires assisted ventilation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h5)

question: Where should the pulse oximeter sensor be placed to obtain an accurate pre-ductal reading?

options.A: Right thigh or calf
options.B: Right wrist or hand
options.C: Left wrist or hand
options.D: Left ankle or foot

explanation: The right arm receives blood directly from the aorta before the ductus arteriosus, showing oxygen levels reaching the brain. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h5)

question: What is the correct compression-to-ventilation ratio during neonatal resuscitation?

options.A: 15 to 2
options.B: 30 to 2
options.C: 3 to 1
options.D: 5 to 1

explanation: Neonates require ninety compressions coordinated with thirty breaths each minute, maintaining a strict 3:1 ratio. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h6)

question: When should chest compressions be started during the resuscitation of a newborn?

options.A: Heart rate below 60 despite effective PPV
options.B: Systolic blood pressure below 40 mmHg
options.C: Absence of breathing within 10 seconds of birth
options.D: Heart rate below 100 despite tactile stimulation

explanation: Compressions are reserved for severe bradycardia that persists after ensuring adequate lung inflation with PPV. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h6)

question: What is the primary cause of bradycardia in a newly born infant?

options.A: Inadequate lung expansion
options.B: Primary cardiac arrest
options.C: Severe congenital heart disease
options.D: Maternal anesthetic toxicity

explanation: Most newborn heart rate drops stem from lack of oxygen due to poor lung aeration rather than heart disease. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h7)

question: Which medication is indicated if the newborn heart rate stays below 60 beats per minute after chest compressions?

options.A: Sodium bicarbonate
options.B: Atropine
options.C: Epinephrine
options.D: Calcium gluconate

explanation: Epinephrine is the primary drug used to stimulate myocardial contractility and heart rate during failed resuscitation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h7)

question: What is the target axillary temperature range for a stabilized newborn after resuscitation?
explanation: Normal body temperature preserves metabolic stability and prevents complications related to cold stress or overheating. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h8)

question: Why is ongoing monitoring essential for infants who required resuscitation at birth?

options.A: They always develop irreversible brain damage
options.B: They lose the ability to maintain blood pressure permanently
options.C: They require lifelong intravenous nutrition
options.D: They are at high risk for delayed clinical deterioration

explanation: Post-resuscitation complications like hypoglycemia, seizures, and respiratory failure can emerge hours after birth. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h8)

question: What is the main challenge a newborn faces right after birth?

options.A: Transitioning from dependent to independent life systems
options.B: Developing immediate immune tolerance
options.C: Adapting to high dietary protein requirements
options.D: Regulating high systemic blood pressure

explanation: The newborn must rapidly shift from relying on maternal placental support to functioning independently with working lungs, gut, and metabolic systems. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h1)

question: Why does immediate newborn care focus mostly on breathing and body temperature?

options.A: Routine hospital protocols mandate recording these first
options.B: They are the easiest parameters to chart in the delivery room
options.C: These are the two systems that fail most frequently during birth transition
options.D: Maternal antibodies cannot protect these organs during the first hour

explanation: Failure to breathe or maintain temperature leads quickly to hypoxia, acidosis, and severe metabolic instability if not immediately corrected. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h1)

question: At what specific times is the Apgar score routinely checked in a newborn?

options.A: One and five minutes after birth
options.B: At birth and one hour post-delivery
options.C: Immediately and ten minutes after birth
options.D: Five and fifteen minutes after birth

explanation: Standard clinical practice requires assessing the newborn at one and five minutes to evaluate initial transition and subsequent stability. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h2)

question: What is an important limitation of using the Apgar score in the delivery room?

options.A: It fails to account for normal gestational age variations
options.B: It only measures neurological damage from birth trauma
options.C: It must not be used to delay urgent resuscitation efforts
options.D: It cannot be accurately calculated by nursing personnel

explanation: Resuscitation starts immediately based on heart rate and breathing status, long before the one-minute Apgar score is finalized. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h2)

question: Which part of a newborn's airway should be suctioned first using a bulb syringe?

options.A: Nose
options.B: Trachea
options.C: Mouth
options.D: Pharynx

explanation: Suctioning the mouth first prevents the infant from gasping and aspirating pooled oral secretions when the nose is subsequently stimulated. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h3)

question: Why should vigorous and deep suctioning of a newborn's throat be avoided?

options.A: It causes immediate closure of the vocal cords
options.B: It can trigger a reflex drop in heart rate
options.C: It prevents the lungs from expanding with air
options.D: It permanently damages the delicate nasal mucosa

explanation: Irritating the posterior pharynx stimulates the vagal nerve, which can lead to severe bradycardia in the newborn. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h3)

question: How do healthy term newborns mainly generate body heat when they are cold?

options.A: Involuntary skeletal muscle shivering
options.B: Rapid peripheral blood vessel dilation
options.C: Increased voluntary muscular activity
options.D: Metabolism of brown adipose tissue

explanation: Newborns cannot shiver effectively and rely instead on breaking down specialized brown fat stores to produce non-shivering heat. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h4)

question: How does drying a newborn immediately after birth help prevent heat loss?

options.A: It stops heat loss caused by evaporation of amniotic fluid
options.B: It blocks convective air currents from chilling wet skin
options.C: It prevents radiant heat transfer from cold delivery room walls
options.D: It eliminates conductive heat transfer from the delivery table

explanation: As residual amniotic fluid turns from liquid to gas on the infant's skin, it draws significant body heat away through evaporation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h4)

question: What condition is routine eye medication given to newborns to prevent?

options.A: Dacryocystitis
options.B: Ophthalmia neonatorum
options.C: Retinopathy of prematurity
options.D: Congenital cataracts

explanation: Routine prophylactic eye ointment protects the newborn's eyes from bacterial infections acquired during passage through the birth canal. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h5)

question: Why is erythromycin eye ointment preferred over older silver nitrate solutions?

options.A: It prevents systemic chlamydial pneumonia infections
options.B: It provides immunity against viral respiratory infections
options.C: It does not cause severe chemical conjunctivitis
options.D: It requires multiple daily doses to remain effective

explanation: Silver nitrate frequently caused painful chemical irritation and discharge, whereas erythromycin is much gentler while remaining effective. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h5)

question: What is the primary reason for giving a vitamin K injection to a newborn?

options.A: Stimulating the production of red blood cells
options.B: Boosting immature cellular immunity
options.C: Preventing hemorrhagic disease of the newborn
options.D: Preventing severe neonatal jaundice

explanation: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting factors, and newborns lack the intestinal bacteria needed to produce it naturally. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h6)

question: Which muscle is the correct site for giving a vitamin K injection to a term newborn?

options.A: Dorsogluteal muscle in the lower back
options.B: Deltoid muscle in the upper arm
options.C: Rectus abdominis muscle in the belly
options.D: Vastus lateralis muscle in the thigh

explanation: The vastus lateralis is well-developed in newborns and avoids major nerves and blood vessels found in other injection sites. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h6)

question: When should identification bands be placed on a newborn?

options.A: After the infant is admitted to the nursery
options.B: When the Apgar score is officially recorded
options.C: Before the infant leaves the delivery room
options.D: Following the first successful breastfeeding session

explanation: Applying ID bands immediately ensures positive identification and prevents infant abduction or mix-ups in the facility. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h7)

question: Which landmarks are used when measuring a newborn's head circumference?

options.A: Across the bridge of the nose and behind the ears
options.B: Just above the eyebrows and around the occipital bone
options.C: Around the forehead line and down to the chin
options.D: Directly over the fontanelles from front to back

explanation: Measuring at the widest occipitofrontal diameter gives an accurate reading of brain growth and detects conditions like hydrocephalus. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h7)

question: What is the recommended minimum time for initial skin-to-skin contact right after birth?

options.A: Until the first bath is given
options.B: At least one hour
options.C: Until the cord falls off
options.D: Exactly fifteen minutes

explanation: The first hour provides a critical window of alertness where transition stabilizes and the infant naturally initiates breastfeeding. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h8)

question: What is a main benefit of early colostrum intake for a newborn?

options.A: Supplying high levels of long-chain fatty acids for growth
options.B: Ensuring immediate closure of the ductus arteriosus
options.C: Providing a rapid source of complete protein for muscle bulk
options.D: Providing high concentrations of protective antibodies

explanation: Colostrum is rich in immunoglobulins that coat the naive mucosal lining of the infant gut, offering crucial defense against pathogens. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h8)

question: How many blood vessels should a normal umbilical cord contain?

options.A: Two vessels
options.B: One vessel
options.C: Four vessels
options.D: Three vessels

explanation: A normal umbilical cord contains two arteries and one vein; a single umbilical artery is sometimes associated with congenital anomalies. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h9)

question: Why is checking the umbilical cord clamp before transfer an important nursing duty?

options.A: To keep the plastic clamp from scratching the mother
options.B: To ensure the cord stump dries and falls off faster
options.C: To stop the flow of blood back into the placenta
options.D: To prevent potential postpartum hemorrhage from the newborn

explanation: An unsecured or loose cord clamp can lead to rapid blood loss and life-threatening hypovolemia in a newborn. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T011#GNS226_U3_T011_h9)

question: What is the standard duration of the puerperium period?

options.A: Six weeks
options.B: Nine months
options.C: Three months
options.D: Fourteen days

explanation: The puerperium spans forty-two days or six weeks, allowing the mother's body to return to the pre-pregnant state. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T012#GNS226_U3_T012_h1)

question: The primary clinical focus during the puerperium is...

options.A: restoring baseline abdominal muscle strength rapidly
options.B: ensuring rapid weight gain for the mother
options.C: monitoring maternal recovery and preventing complications
options.D: initiating immediate weaning from breast milk

explanation: Postnatal care centers heavily on observing physiological changes and catching early signs of postpartum illness. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T012#GNS226_U3_T012_h1)

question: A bright red postpartum uterine discharge occurring on the second day is called what?

options.A: Lochia alba
options.B: Lochia purulenta
options.C: Lochia serosa
options.D: Lochia rubra

explanation: Lochia rubra is the initial red discharge seen in the first few days after childbirth. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T012#GNS226_U3_T012_h2)

question: What finding indicates delayed uterine involution during a postnatal ward check?

options.A: The fundus remains soft and high above the umbilicus
options.B: The fundus is firm and located below the symphysis pubis
options.C: Lochia transitions from red to white by day ten
options.D: Mild cramping occurs during infant breastfeeding

explanation: A high, boggy uterus indicates poor contraction and points toward potential postpartum hemorrhage or retained products. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T012#GNS226_U3_T012_h2)

question: Which hormone is chiefly responsible for the milk ejection reflex during suckling?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Progesterone
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Oxytocin stimulates smooth muscle contraction in the breast ducts, forcing milk out for the baby. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T012#GNS226_U3_T012_h3)

question: Why is colostrum considered uniquely beneficial for a newborn baby?

options.A: It acts as a strong chemical laxative to clear kidneys
options.B: It contains high concentrations of protective antibodies
options.C: It prevents the infant from losing any birth weight
options.D: It provides high levels of dietary fat for rapid sleep

explanation: Colostrum delivers vital immunological protection and antibodies before mature milk comes in. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T012#GNS226_U3_T012_h3)

question: A postpartum temperature reading of 38.5°C on the third day most likely indicates...

options.A: milk let-down
options.B: dehydration
options.C: normal stress
options.D: infection

explanation: Any fever above 38°C after the first twenty-four hours suggests puerperal sepsis or another localized infection. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T012#GNS226_U3_T012_h4)

question: What is the clinical significance of a boggy, deviated uterine fundus?

options.A: A full bladder is displacing the uterus and preventing contraction
options.B: Normal hormonal fluctuations are shifting pelvic organ alignment
options.C: The placenta has successfully delivered without retained fragments
options.D: The mother is experiencing standard postpartum uterine cramping

explanation: A distended bladder pushes the uterine corpus sideways and stops it from contracting effectively. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T012#GNS226_U3_T012_h4)

question: Which symptom characterizes the temporary condition known as maternity blues?

options.A: Mild tearfulness and mood swings in the first week
options.B: Severe suicidal ideation requiring hospital admission
options.C: Total rejection of the infant lasting many months
options.D: Auditory hallucinations and detachment from reality

explanation: Maternity blues are mild, short-lived emotional fluctuations that clear up spontaneously within days. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T012#GNS226_U3_T012_h5)

question: How do maternity blues differ fundamentally from postpartum depression?

options.A: Blues require antipsychotic drug therapy, while depression needs simple nutritional support
options.B: Blues only occur after cesarean delivery, while depression follows normal vaginal delivery
options.C: Blues resolve on their own quickly, while depression persists and impairs daily function
options.D: Depression features physical pain, whereas blues involve only hormonal headaches

explanation: The key differentiator is duration and severity, with depression interfering with normal caregiving abilities. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T012#GNS226_U3_T012_h5)

question: Which finding is classified as a red flag during postnatal home visits?

options.A: Foul-smelling vaginal discharge and fever
options.B: Mild lower abdominal cramping during feeds
options.C: Transient night sweats in the first week
options.D: Pinkish lochia serosa on day six

explanation: Foul lochia combined with fever points straight to uterine infection or puerperal sepsis. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T012#GNS226_U3_T012_h6)

question: A postpartum mother complains of unilateral calf swelling, tenderness, and warmth. What is the suspected condition?

options.A: Postpartum eclampsia
options.B: Normal muscular fatigue
options.C: Deep vein thrombosis
options.D: Superficial mastitis

explanation: One-sided leg swelling, pain, and warmth strongly suggest a deep vein clot requiring urgent medical review. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T012#GNS226_U3_T012_h6)

question: Why are combined oral contraceptives generally delayed in early breastfeeding mothers?

options.A: They can diminish milk supply and increase clot risks
options.B: They instantly cause permanent cessation of ovulation
options.C: They transfer heavy toxic metals into the breastmilk
options.D: They prevent the normal process of uterine involution

explanation: Estrogen in combined pills can suppress lactation and heighten the risk of blood clots. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T012#GNS226_U3_T012_h7)

question: What is the main requirement for the Lactational Amenorrhea Method to work effectively?

options.A: Automatic resumption of normal menstrual cycles
options.B: Complete absence of lochia discharge for six weeks
options.C: Exclusive and frequent breastfeeding without supplementary feeds
options.D: Maternal consumption of high-protein local Nigerian diets

explanation: LAM relies on continuous, exclusive suckling to suppress ovulation and hormonal release. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T012#GNS226_U3_T012_h7)

question: What is the standard duration of the puerperium period in clinical practice?

options.A: Two weeks
options.B: Six weeks
options.C: Ten days
options.D: Three months

explanation: The puerperium typically lasts for six weeks, during which the maternal body returns to its pre-pregnant state. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h1)

question: The immediate puerperium refers to which specific timeframe after delivery?

options.A: Weeks four to six
options.B: The first 24 hours
options.C: The second week
options.D: Days two to seven

explanation: The immediate puerperium covers the first 24 hours post-delivery, which is the highest risk window for hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h1)

question: What is the medical term for the shrinking of the uterus back to its normal size?

options.A: Subinvolution
options.B: Atrophy
options.C: Autolysis
options.D: Involution

explanation: Involution is the physiological process where the postpartum uterus returns to its pre-pregnancy size and condition. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h2)

question: A postpartum client's uterus fails to decrease in size as expected. What is this condition called?

options.A: Atresia
options.B: Subinvolution
options.C: Inversion
options.D: Involution

explanation: Subinvolution occurs when the uterus does not properly return to its normal size, often due to retained tissue or infection. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h2)

question: What color is lochia serosa when assessed during the first week postpartum?

options.A: Dark green
options.B: Yellowish-white
options.C: Pinkish-brown
options.D: Bright red

explanation: Lochia serosa transitions to a paler, pinkish-brown color between days five and nine as the bleeding diminishes. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h3)

question: A foul-smelling lochia discharge in a postpartum patient is a primary indicator of what condition?

options.A: Mastitis
options.B: Endometritis
options.C: Cystitis
options.D: Normal involution

explanation: An unpleasant odor in lochia points toward an infection of the uterine lining, known clinically as endometritis. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h3)

question: What physiological process helps the body eliminate excess pregnancy fluid via heavy urination?

options.A: Involution
options.B: Diaphoresis
options.C: Dialysis
options.D: Diuresis

explanation: Diuresis is the increased production of urine that allows the body to rid itself of excess extracellular fluid accumulated during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h4)

question: What vital sign change is considered an early warning sign of postpartum hemorrhage?

options.A: Normal pulse and high temperature
options.B: Slow pulse and normal blood pressure
options.C: Rapid pulse and falling blood pressure
options.D: Slow pulse and high blood pressure

explanation: A rising heart rate coupled with dropping blood pressure indicates significant internal or external blood loss. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h4)

question: What is the name of the nutrient-rich fluid produced by the breasts in the first few days after birth?

options.A: Chyle
options.B: Serum
options.C: Lochia
options.D: Colostrum

explanation: Colostrum is the initial yellowish milk secretion packed with vital immune globulins for the newborn. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h5)

question: When does mature milk production typically replace colostrum in the postpartum mother?

options.A: At the end of week six
options.B: After one month
options.C: Immediately at birth
options.D: Day three to five

explanation: Copious milk production usually begins between the third and fifth day following delivery due to changing hormone levels. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h5)

question: What is the typical timeframe for the spontaneous resolution of the baby blues?

options.A: Forty-eight hours
options.B: Two weeks
options.C: Three months
options.D: Six weeks

explanation: Baby blues are short-lived emotional episodes that typically resolve on their own within the first two weeks postpartum. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h6)

question: A mother experiences severe tearfulness, anxiety, and mood swings that persist past four weeks. What is the likely condition?

options.A: Postnatal psychosis
options.B: Involutional melancholia
options.C: Baby blues
options.D: Postpartum depression

explanation: Symptoms lasting beyond two weeks and impairing daily activities point toward postpartum depression rather than transient baby blues. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h6)

question: What is the correct direction for a postpartum mother to clean her perineum to prevent infection?

options.A: Back to front
options.B: In circular motions
options.C: Front to back
options.D: Side to side

explanation: Wiping or washing from front to back prevents the transfer of fecal bacteria into the vaginal and urethral areas. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h7)

question: Why is early ambulation encouraged for women who have experienced an uncomplicated vaginal delivery?

options.A: To increase lochia production
options.B: To prevent deep vein thrombosis
options.C: To accelerate uterine involution directly
options.D: To suppress milk engorgement

explanation: Moving around early improves lower extremity circulation, reducing the risk of blood clots forming in the veins. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h7)

question: What three rapid parameters are checked immediately after a baby is born?

options.A: Gestational age, breathing, and muscle tone
options.B: Heart rate, weight, and temperature
options.C: Skin color, cry strength, and blood pressure
options.D: Length, head circumference, and reflexes

explanation: Evaluating gestational age, respiratory effort, and muscle tone instantly tells the nurse if the newborn needs routine care or immediate resuscitation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h1)

question: A newborn is limp and not breathing at birth. What is the immediate nursing action?

options.A: Weigh the infant before starting any procedures
options.B: Take the baby straight to the mother's bed
options.C: Move the baby to a radiant warmer for resuscitation
options.D: Bathe the baby quickly with warm water

explanation: Poor tone and absent breathing require moving the newborn to a warm resuscitation area to establish effective ventilation without delay. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h1)

question: At what specific time intervals is the Apgar score routinely assessed?

options.A: Immediately and at 10 minutes
options.B: 5 and 15 minutes after delivery
options.C: At birth and every hour for two hours
options.D: 1 and 5 minutes after birth

explanation: Apgar scoring is performed at one minute to gauge tolerance of birth and at five minutes to assess adaptation to the extrauterine environment. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h2)

question: An Apgar score of 5 at one minute indicates what clinical status in a newborn?

options.A: Severe distress requiring immediate intubation
options.B: Normal transition with no need for action
options.C: Extreme prematurity regardless of breathing
options.D: Moderate distress requiring supportive care

explanation: Scores between 4 and 6 reflect moderate depression, meaning the newborn needs careful monitoring and respiratory support such as stimulation or oxygen. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h2)

question: Drying a newborn immediately after birth prevents which primary method of heat loss?

options.A: Evaporation
options.B: Convection
options.C: Radiation
options.D: Conduction

explanation: As amniotic fluid evaporates from the wet newborn skin, it draws heat away, making thorough drying essential right after birth. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h3)

question: Why does placing an unheated metal stethoscope directly on a newborn's chest risk heat loss?

options.A: It causes conductive heat transfer from the baby to the cold metal
options.B: It speeds up evaporative heat loss through the wet skin pores
options.C: It blocks radiant heat from reaching the baby from the room walls
options.D: It creates convective air currents that cool the surrounding skin

explanation: Direct contact between the warm newborn skin and a colder solid object results in conductive heat loss. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of administering Vitamin K to a newborn?

options.A: To prevent bleeding disorders due to clotting factor deficiencies
options.B: To stimulate early meconium passage and gut motility
options.C: To protect the infant eyes from bacterial eye infections
options.D: To build active immunity against viral hepatitis B

explanation: Newborns have sterile intestines and cannot produce clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X, making Vitamin K essential to prevent hemorrhagic disease. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h4)

question: Why is tetracycline eye ointment applied to the eyes of all newborns shortly after delivery?

options.A: To treat existing congenital cataracts found during the first exam
options.B: To prevent ophthalmia neonatorum from maternal sexually transmitted infections
options.C: To prevent irritation from routine antiseptic skin cleansing
options.D: To lubricate dry corneas caused by bright delivery room lights

explanation: Eye prophylaxis protects the infant from gonorrheal and chlamydial organisms present in the birth canal, preventing severe corneal damage. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h4)

question: What is the primary benefit of the thick yellowish colostrum produced in the first days?

options.A: It replaces the need for routine vitamin K injections
options.B: It supplies high amounts of fat for rapid weight gain
options.C: It acts as a strong sedative to keep the baby sleeping
options.D: It provides essential antibodies and helps clear meconium

explanation: Colostrum is rich in immunoglobulins and has mild laxative effects that assist in passing the first dark stools and clearing bilirubin. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h5)

question: Which nursing action best ensures successful breastfeeding technique during early feeds?

options.A: Guiding the baby to take a large portion of the areola into the mouth
options.B: Placing the nipple directly inside the center of the baby's lips
options.C: Feeding the baby on a strict schedule every four hours
options.D: Supplementing with glucose water if the mother is tired

explanation: A deep latch that includes the areola protects the maternal nipple from trauma and allows the baby to compress the milk ducts effectively. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h5)

question: How many blood vessels should a normal umbilical cord contain upon inspection?

options.A: One artery and one vein
options.B: Two veins and one artery
options.C: Two arteries and one vein
options.D: Two arteries and two veins

explanation: A normal umbilical cord has three vessels: two smaller arteries carrying deoxygenated blood and one larger vein carrying oxygenated blood. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h6)

question: What finding during the physical examination requires immediate reporting to the doctor?

options.A: Brick-red staining on the wet diaper
options.B: A tuft of hair over the lower lumbar spine
options.C: A slight soft swelling across the suture lines
options.D: Milia scattered across the newborn's nose

explanation: Spinal tufts, dimples, or skin tags can indicate underlying neural tube defects like spina bifida occulta requiring further evaluation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h6)

question: What are the small white papules commonly found on a newborn's nose and chin called?

options.A: Erythema toxicum
options.B: Milia
options.C: Lanugo
options.D: Mongolian spots

explanation: Milia are distended sebaceous glands that appear as tiny white spots on the face and disappear without any treatment. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h7)

question: A mother is worried about flat, dark bluish-gray patches on her baby's lower back. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Suggest immediate blood tests to check for liver disease
options.B: Explain that these are Mongolian spots and usually fade over time
options.C: Report the finding urgently as a sign of severe internal bruising
options.D: Apply medicated ointment to prevent the spots from spreading

explanation: Mongolian spots are harmless pigmented birthmarks common in infants with darker skin tones and require no intervention. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a general danger sign in a newborn?

options.A: Chest indrawing and very rapid breathing
options.B: Inability to breastfeed or suckle well
options.C: Body temperature that is abnormally low
options.D: Passing meconium within the first 24 hours

explanation: Passing meconium early in life is a normal physiological milestone, whereas poor feeding, coldness, and respiratory distress are clear danger signs. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h8)

question: A newborn presents with yellow skin discoloration that reaches the palms and soles on the second day of life. What does this indicate?

options.A: A harmless reaction to newborn eye prophylaxis
options.B: Normal physiologic jaundice that will resolve alone
options.C: Inadequate intake of plain drinking water
options.D: Pathological jaundice requiring prompt investigation

explanation: Jaundice appearing on the first day or spreading to the palms and soles suggests high bilirubin levels that are abnormal and require treatment. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h8)

question: What is the recommended method for routine umbilical cord care at home?

options.A: Applying traditional herbal concoctions to speed up drying
options.B: Washing the stump daily with soapy bath water
options.C: Covering the cord tightly with an airtight adhesive bandage
options.D: Keeping the cord clean and dry without applying substances

explanation: Dry cord care prevents infection and tetanus by avoiding harmful traditional applications such as saliva, ash, or dirty oils. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h9)

question: Why is it important to educate mothers in Nigeria about exclusive breastfeeding before discharge?

options.A: To ensure the baby sleeps through the night without waking
options.B: To help the mother lose pregnancy weight much faster
options.C: To replace the need for routine childhood immunizations
options.D: To prevent early introduction of water and foods that cause infections

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding provides all necessary nutrients and protective antibodies while shielding the infant from contaminated waterborne pathogens. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h9)

question: What is the recommended duration for exclusive breastfeeding by global health standards?

options.A: First nine months
options.B: First six months
options.C: First twelve months
options.D: First three months

explanation: Global health guidelines strongly advocate for exclusive breastfeeding during the initial half-year of life. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h1)

question: Why should a strictly breastfed infant not be given plain water during the first six months?

options.A: Water increases the risk of contamination and illness
options.B: Water ruins the infant's natural taste buds
options.C: Water prevents the mother from making enough milk
options.D: Water causes the infant to sleep for too long

explanation: Unboiled or contaminated water introduces harmful bacteria to the immature digestive tract, leading to diarrhea. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h1)

question: Which hormone is primarily responsible for the actual synthesis or production of milk?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Prolactin

explanation: Prolactin acts directly on the alveolar cells within the mammary glands to stimulate milk production. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h2)

question: A nursing mother complains that her milk only flows after the baby sucks for a minute. What explains this?

options.A: Inhibition of progesterone by infant saliva
options.B: The milk ejection reflex triggered by oxytocin
options.C: Prolactin accumulation in the milk ducts
options.D: Alveolar breakdown releasing stored nutrients

explanation: Baby suckling triggers the release of oxytocin, which makes the muscles around the milk glands contract and push the milk down the ducts. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h2)

question: What is the primary immunological component found in high concentration in colostrum?

options.A: Platelet-derived growth factor
options.B: Fibrinogen strands
options.C: Red blood cells
options.D: Secretory IgA

explanation: Colostrum is rich in secretory IgA, creating a protective barrier along the newborn's mucosal surfaces. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h3)

question: How does the carbohydrate content in breast milk help the newborn?

options.A: It acts as a mild sedative to encourage sleeping
options.B: It accelerates the closure of the ductus arteriosus
options.C: It hardens the tooth enamel before eruption
options.D: It promotes the growth of beneficial gut bacteria

explanation: Lactose and other sugars in breast milk help good bacteria grow in the baby's digestive tract while keeping harmful bacteria away. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h3)

question: How does immediate breastfeeding help reduce the risk of postpartum hemorrhage?

options.A: By stimulating uterine contractions through oxytocin release
options.B: By increasing systemic blood pressure
options.C: By thinning the circulating blood volume
options.D: By promoting rapid clotting factor synthesis in the liver

explanation: Suckling triggers oxytocin release, causing the uterus to contract and clamp down on bleeding placental sites. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h4)

question: Why does exclusive breastfeeding act as a natural method to prevent pregnancy after birth?

options.A: It thickens the cervical mucus permanently
options.B: It suppresses the hormonal signals required for ovulation
options.C: It induces chemical changes that destroy sperm
options.D: It causes the womb lining to shed continuously

explanation: Frequent suckling stops the body from releasing the hormones needed to produce eggs. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h4)

question: When is the ideal time to initiate breastfeeding after a normal vaginal delivery?

options.A: Once the milk transitions from colostrum
options.B: Within the first hour
options.C: After the infant receives initial immunizations
options.D: After twelve hours of rest

explanation: Early initiation capitalizes on the infant's strong suckling instinct right after birth. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h5)

question: What sign shows that a baby has latched on properly during a feed?

options.A: Only the tip of the nipple is inside the mouth
options.B: The infant's lips are inverted inward
options.C: More areola is visible above the top lip than below
options.D: The mother experiences sharp pain with every suck

explanation: A good latch includes more of the lower areola in the baby's mouth so the milk ducts are compressed properly. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h5)

question: What is the primary cause of sore and cracked nipples in a breastfeeding mother?

options.A: Excessive water intake
options.B: Inadequate infant attachment
options.C: Frequent diaper changes
options.D: High maternal protein consumption

explanation: Poor latching forces the infant to suck on the nipple tip instead of taking in the areola, causing tissue trauma. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h6)

question: A mother presents with a hard, red, painful breast and a temperature of 38.5 degrees Celsius. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Encourage continued milk removal and prompt medical referral
options.B: Recommend restricting fluid intake to dry up the milk
options.C: Apply tight compression bandage to reduce swelling
options.D: Advise immediate cessation of feeding from both breasts

explanation: Continuing to remove milk helps clear blockages and prevents infection from worsening, while a doctor evaluates for mastitis treatment. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h6)

question: How long can freshly expressed breast milk safely remain at room temperature?

options.A: Up to one week
options.B: Up to twenty-four hours
options.C: Up to forty-eight hours
options.D: Up to four hours

explanation: Fresh breast milk contains antibacterial properties that keep it safe at room temperature for a limited period. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h7)

question: Why should you avoid using a microwave oven to warm frozen breast milk?

options.A: It causes the milk to curdle instantly
options.B: It destroys immunological properties and creates dangerous hot spots
options.C: It adds toxic chemicals from the plastic container
options.D: It alters the color of the milk permanently

explanation: Microwaving heats milk unevenly, creating hot spots that can burn the baby's mouth, and destroys important nutrients. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h7)

question: What is an important nursing responsibility during pregnancy regarding infant feeding?

options.A: Providing education and addressing potential concerns
options.B: Measuring the infant's birth weight in advance
options.C: Administering prophylactic antibiotics to the mother
options.D: Prescribing routine milk supplements for home use

explanation: Antenatal teaching helps mothers learn breastfeeding basics and builds their confidence before the baby arrives. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h8)

question: Which nursing action best supports exclusive breastfeeding right after delivery?

options.A: Assisting with early skin-to-skin contact and correct latching
options.B: Separating the mother and infant to allow maternal rest
options.C: Instructing the mother to feed strictly by the clock
options.D: Providing formula supplements to prevent weight loss

explanation: Skin-to-skin contact and a correct latch help stimulate milk supply and make feeding easier for both mother and baby. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T015#GNS226_U3_T015_h8)

question: How many weeks does the postnatal period typically last after childbirth?

options.A: Three months
options.B: Six weeks
options.C: Two weeks
options.D: Six months

explanation: The puerperium spans forty-two days, which equals six weeks of postpartum physiological recovery. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h1)

question: Why is early postnatal monitoring important in busy healthcare facilities?

options.A: Fathers must remain admitted alongside the mother for support
options.B: Routine lab tests must be completed daily without exception
options.C: Babies need immediate formal schooling enrollment during this phase
options.D: Mothers often discharge early, requiring urgent education before they leave

explanation: Early discharge protocols require quick and effective teaching while the mother is still in the facility. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h1)

question: What is the term for the normal shrinkage of the uterus after childbirth?

options.A: Subinvolution
options.B: Involution
options.C: Atrophy
options.D: Lochia

explanation: Involution refers specifically to the postpartum reduction in uterine size back to pre-pregnancy dimensions. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h2)

question: By what timeframe should the shrinking uterus no longer be palpable abdominally?

options.A: Three days
options.B: Twenty-four hours
options.C: Six weeks
options.D: Ten days

explanation: By about the tenth postpartum day, the uterus descends completely into the true pelvis and is no longer felt abdominally. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h2)

question: How often should vital signs and uterine tone be checked during the first hour after birth?

options.A: Once every hour
options.B: Every two hours
options.C: Every fifteen minutes
options.D: Every thirty minutes

explanation: Immediate postpartum monitoring requires checking vitals and uterine consistency every fifteen minutes at first to catch bleeding early. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h3)

question: A postpartum mother has a soft, displaced uterus and heavy bleeding. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Encourage the mother to walk around
options.B: Administer oral iron supplements
options.C: Perform immediate fundal massage
options.D: Prepare the patient for immediate discharge

explanation: Massaging a soft uterus stimulates muscle fibers to contract, which closes open blood vessels and reduces bleeding. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h3)

question: When does the final routine postnatal check-up usually happen?

options.A: At fourteen days
options.B: At three months
options.C: At twenty-four hours
options.D: At six weeks

explanation: The six-week visit serves as the main final check for physical and emotional recovery. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h4)

question: Which finding during a routine check of the perineum needs prompt medical attention?

options.A: Mild pulling sensations during sitting
options.B: Foul-smelling discharge and severe pain
options.C: A closed, healing skin line
options.D: Mild swelling present on day two

explanation: Foul discharge and severe pain point toward an infection or a blood clot in the tissue that needs treatment. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h4)

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for milk release, known as the let-down reflex?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Oxytocin triggers the contraction of tiny muscles around the milk glands, forcing milk down into the ducts. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h5)

question: What is the best initial nursing intervention for managing painful breast engorgement?

options.A: Restrict maternal fluid intake significantly
options.B: Encourage frequent breastfeeding or milk expression
options.C: Apply tight bandages to suppress milk production
options.D: Advise the mother to stop feeding for two days

explanation: Emptying the breasts regularly relieves pressure, prevents stasis, and keeps milk production flowing smoothly. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h5)

question: What is the amount of blood loss used to diagnose postpartum hemorrhage after a normal vaginal delivery?

options.A: 200 milliliters
options.B: 500 milliliters
options.C: 1500 milliliters
options.D: 1000 milliliters

explanation: Vaginal blood loss above 500ml within the first 24 hours is classified as a postpartum hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h6)

question: Which clinical sign points most directly toward a developing uterine infection?

options.A: Unilateral leg calf tenderness
options.B: Mild postpartum fatigue
options.C: Transient emotional tearfulness
options.D: Fever and foul-smelling lochia

explanation: Fever combined with bad-smelling vaginal discharge indicates an infection inside the uterus that requires antibiotics. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h6)

question: What is a common feature of the mild emotional condition known as 'baby blues'?

options.A: Uncontrolled hallucinations about the baby
options.B: Spontaneous resolution within two weeks
options.C: Permanent requirement for psychiatric medications
options.D: Complete refusal to feed the newborn

explanation: Baby blues are mild mood swings that go away on their own as hormone levels settle down. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h7)

question: How does postpartum depression differ from the mild baby blues?

options.A: It only affects mothers who experience surgical deliveries
options.B: It lasts longer and gets in the way of daily life
options.C: It resolves entirely within the first twenty-four hours
options.D: It exclusively occurs before the delivery of the placenta

explanation: Postpartum depression persists and interferes with the mother's ability to care for herself and her child. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h7)

question: Why should iron supplements usually continue after childbirth?

options.A: To stimulate immediate uterine involution
options.B: To replace blood lost during childbirth
options.C: To prevent the development of infant rickets
options.D: To enhance the taste of breast milk

explanation: Continued iron intake helps rebuild blood levels that were lowered during pregnancy and delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h8)

question: What is the correct way to teach mothers to clean their perineal area after birth?

options.A: Avoid washing the area until sutures dissolve
options.B: Use harsh antiseptic soaps multiple times daily
options.C: Wipe or wash from front to back
options.D: Scrub the episiotomy wound with a dry towel

explanation: Cleaning from front to back stops bacteria from the anus from spreading to the healing wound. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h8)

question: What is the earliest time a woman can start ovulating again after childbirth?

options.A: Three weeks
options.B: One year
options.C: Six months
options.D: Forty days

explanation: A woman can release an egg and get pregnant before her first menstrual period returns, sometimes as early as three weeks. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h9)

question: Why are progestin-only contraceptives preferred over combined pills for breastfeeding mothers?

options.A: They guarantee permanent sterilization after one dose
options.B: They cure postpartum depression within days
options.C: They completely eliminate the need for future immunizations
options.D: They do not interfere with established milk supply

explanation: Progestin-only options do not contain estrogen, making them safe to use while nursing without reducing milk production. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h9)

question: Which vaccines are usually given to a newborn before leaving the hospital?

options.A: Hepatitis A and meningococcal
options.B: Yellow fever and typhoid
options.C: Tetanus toxoid and measles
options.D: BCG and oral polio vaccine

explanation: The BCG vaccine and oral polio drops are standard immunizations given to newborns right after birth. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h10)

question: What is the main purpose of community health worker home visits during the postnatal period?

options.A: To collect hospital user fees from the family
options.B: To bridge hospital care and home by checking on recovery
options.C: To perform surgical repairs of torn perineums
options.D: To supply the household with adult food rations

explanation: Home visits help ensure ongoing support, catch any problems early, and make sure immunizations are kept on track. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h10)

question: What pigment is responsible for the yellow discoloration in neonatal jaundice?

options.A: Bilirubin
options.B: Creatinine
options.C: Hemoglobin
options.D: Albumin

explanation: Bilirubin is the yellow breakdown product of normal heme catabolism that accumulates in the skin and sclera. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h1)

question: Why is jaundice particularly common in newborn infants?

options.A: Their red blood cells have a very long lifespan
options.B: They consume excessive amounts of breast milk
options.C: Their kidneys fail to excrete clear urine
options.D: Their liver function is temporarily immature

explanation: Neonates have immature liver enzymes that cannot conjugate and clear bilirubin as quickly as older children. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h1)

question: Which enzyme is responsible for conjugating bilirubin inside the liver?

options.A: Amylase
options.B: Glucuronyl transferase
options.C: Lipase
options.D: Transaminase

explanation: Glucuronyl transferase is the key hepatic enzyme that attaches glucuronic acid to unconjugated bilirubin to make it water-soluble. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h2)

question: What property makes unconjugated bilirubin hazardous to the central nervous system?

options.A: It is fat-soluble and crosses cell membranes easily
options.B: It blocks the normal flow of cerebrospinal fluid
options.C: It destroys circulating blood platelets rapidly
options.D: It reacts violently with normal stomach acid

explanation: Unconjugated bilirubin is lipophilic, allowing it to cross the blood-brain barrier and deposit in brain tissue. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h2)

question: When does physiological jaundice typically first become visible?

options.A: Immediately at birth
options.B: At two weeks of age
options.C: After 24 hours of life
options.D: Within the first 2 hours

explanation: Physiological jaundice never appears in the first 24 hours; its onset is delayed until at least the second day of life. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h3)

question: A newborn develops deep yellow skin within the first 6 hours of birth. This finding suggests:

options.A: Inadequate fluid intake from delayed breastfeeding
options.B: Normal physiological adaptation to extrauterine life
options.C: Pathological jaundice requiring immediate investigation
options.D: Harmless reaction to routine vitamin K administration

explanation: Jaundice appearing within the first 24 hours of life is considered pathological until proven otherwise and demands prompt workup. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h3)

question: What inherited enzyme defect is a major risk factor for severe neonatal jaundice in Nigeria?

options.A: Galactosemia
options.B: G6PD deficiency
options.C: Phenylketonuria
options.D: Sickle cell trait

explanation: G6PD deficiency is widespread in the Nigerian population and predisposes newborns to acute hemolysis and severe hyperbilirubinemia. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h4)

question: How does untreated neonatal sepsis contribute to the development of jaundice?

options.A: It impairs liver function and accelerates red blood cell breakdown
options.B: It directly blocks the infant's bile ducts from forming
options.C: It stops the baby from producing protective skin oils
options.D: It causes the kidneys to produce excess conjugated bilirubin

explanation: Systemic infection places metabolic stress on the liver and increases hemolysis, worsening bilirubin accumulation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h4)

question: In what direction does jaundice typically spread across the newborn's body?

options.A: Centrifugal from spine outward
options.B: Acrocaudal from toes to head
options.C: Random patches across the trunk
options.D: Cephalocaudal from head to toe

explanation: Jaundice generally progresses in a head-to-toe direction, with the face showing color changes first. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h5)

question: Why is visual inspection alone considered unreliable for measuring neonatal bilirubin levels?

options.A: Bilirubin only deposits in the sclera and never the skin
options.B: Newborn skin is too thick for bilirubin to show through
options.C: Room lighting never affects how human eyes see color
options.D: Skin pigmentation masks underlying yellow discoloration

explanation: Natural skin tone variations make visual inspection subjective and unreliable, necessitating laboratory confirmation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h5)

question: What is the gold standard diagnostic test for measuring newborn bilirubin levels?

options.A: Transcutaneous skin meter reading
options.B: Direct visual color chart comparison
options.C: Total serum bilirubin blood test
options.D: Routine urinalysis for urobilinogen

explanation: Total serum bilirubin (TSB) obtained from blood samples provides the definitive measurement for clinical decision-making. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h6)

question: What does a positive direct Coombs test on cord blood indicate?

options.A: The infant has an inherited inability to produce liver enzymes
options.B: Antibodies from the mother are attacking the infant's red blood cells
options.C: The newborn is suffering from severe bacterial meningitis
options.D: Bilirubin levels have already crossed into the central nervous system

explanation: A positive direct Coombs test reveals maternal antibodies coating neonatal red blood cells, pointing to immune hemolysis. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h6)

question: What is the primary mechanism of action for phototherapy in newborns?

options.A: Speeding up the infant's heart rate to filter waste
options.B: Killing harmful bacteria that cause blood cell breakdown
options.C: Stimulating the liver to produce more digestive enzymes
options.D: Converting bilirubin into water-soluble isomers for excretion

explanation: Phototherapy uses light energy to change fat-soluble bilirubin into water-soluble photoisomers that the body can excrete without liver conjugation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h7)

question: When is an exchange transfusion typically chosen over standard phototherapy?

options.A: When bilirubin levels reach dangerous thresholds threatening brain damage
options.B: When physiological jaundice appears after the third day of life
options.C: When the infant refuses to breastfeed for more than two hours
options.D: When the mother has a negative blood type without antibodies
